title: Risk of Virological Failure After Switch to a Tenofovir-Sparing Dual Therapy in Virologically Suppressed People With HIV and Past HBV Infection.
abstract: We compared the effectiveness of tenofovir (TFV)-based triple regimens (TT) to TFV-sparing dual therapies (DT) in virologically suppressed, HBsAg-/HBcAb+ people living with HIV (PLWH). We emulated a target trial including adults PLWH from five University Hospitals, with HBsAg-/HBcAb+ serostatus, starting a TT with unsuppressed serum HIV-RNA and reaching HIV-RNA 50 cp/mL or a single HIV-RNA ≥ 200 cp/mL) were estimated through a weighted Kaplan-Meier estimator. Overall, 415 PLWH were eligible for study analysis: 71 (17.1%) started a DT (3TC-based: 78.9%) during follow-up. They were mainly men (329, 79.3%), with a median age of 48 years. In the weighted analysis, the estimated probabilities of VF were: 29.3% for DT and 29.9% for TT at 5 years (difference: 0.5%; 95% CI: -28.7, +21.6). A higher VF risk was seen in the subset of PLWH with undetectable HBsAb at the longest follow-up available (4 years), independently of treatment group: 15.5% and 36.8% with DT and TT, respectively (difference: -21.3%; 95% CI: -30.3, -13.8). Switch to a TFV-sparing DT, compared with continuing a TT, was not associated with an increased risk of VF in PLWH and prior HBV infection.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to compare the effectiveness of tenofovir-based triple regimens to tenofovir-sparing dual therapies in virologically suppressed people living with HIV and past hepatitis B infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was an emulation of a target trial including adults with HIV and HBsAg-/HBcAb+ serostatus from five University Hospitals, comparing tenofovir-based triple regimens to tenofovir-sparing dual therapies.
analysis.methods: The study estimated the probability of virological failure (defined as HIV-RNA > 50 cp/mL or a single HIV-RNA ≥ 200 cp/mL) through a weighted Kaplan-Meier estimator.
analysis.main_results: In the weighted analysis, the estimated probabilities of virological failure were 29.3% for dual therapy and 29.9% for triple therapy at 5 years (difference: 0.5%; 95% CI: -28.7, +21.6).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that switching to a tenofovir-sparing dual therapy was not associated with an increased risk of virological failure compared to continuing a triple therapy in this population.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the use of tenofovir-sparing dual therapies as a viable option for virologically suppressed people with HIV and past HBV infection, potentially reducing long-term tenofovir exposure.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was an emulation of a target trial, which may introduce unmeasured confounding; however, the large sample size and robust statistical methods provide moderate confidence in the results.

analysis.summary_en: This study compared tenofovir-based triple regimens to tenofovir-sparing dual therapies in virologically suppressed people living with HIV and past hepatitis B infection. Among 415 eligible participants, 71 started dual therapy during follow-up. The estimated 5-year probability of virological failure was similar between groups (29.3% for dual therapy vs. 29.9% for triple therapy). A higher virological failure risk was observed in participants with undetectable HBsAb at longest follow-up, but this was independent of treatment group. The findings suggest that switching to tenofovir-sparing dual therapy is not associated with increased virological failure risk in this population.

title: Self-reported hepatitis B vaccination uptake and associated factors among adults in a tertiary hospital, Nasarawa State, Nigeria.
abstract: Background Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major public health challenge in sub-Saharan Africa despite the availability of a safe and effective vaccine. In Nigeria, adult vaccination coverage and completion rates are not well characterized within hospital-based populations. Methods A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 1,200 adults attending Federal Medical Centre (FMC) Keffi, Nasarawa State, Nigeria. Data on socio-demographics, HBV-related knowledge, attitudes, perceived barriers, vaccination uptake, and completion were collected using a structured questionnaire. Knowledge and attitude scores were categorized into poor, fair, and good levels. Associations between socio-demographic characteristics and vaccination uptake were examined using chi-square and Fisher's exact tests, with statistical significance set at p Results The mean age of respondents was predominantly 36-40 years (32.5%), with males constituting 72.3%. Most respondents had tertiary education (91.8%) and were civil servants (83.4%). Overall awareness of HBV was high (95.5%), with a mean knowledge score of 12.37 ± 1.42. Good knowledge was observed in 74.2% of respondents, while 57.2% demonstrated good attitudes toward HBV prevention. Vaccination uptake was high, with 93.5% reporting receipt of at least one vaccine dose. However, only 22.3% had completed the recommended three-dose schedule, while 48.2% and 23.1% had received one and two doses, respectively. Willingness to complete vaccination was reported by 81.6% of respondents. Perceived barriers included high vaccine cost (72.4%), inadequate access to health facilities (96.9%), fear of side effects (71.9%), and insufficient information (73.5%). No significant associations were found between socio-demographic variables and vaccination uptake (p > 0.05 for all). Conclusion Despite high HBV vaccination initiation and knowledge levels, substantial gaps in vaccine completion persist. Addressing financial, informational, and access-related barriers is essential to improve full vaccination coverage among Nigerian adults.
journal: Tropical diseases, travel medicine and vaccines

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对尼日利亚纳萨拉瓦州凯菲联邦医疗中心 (FMC) 的 1,200 名成年人进行了一项以医院为基础的横断面研究。受访者的平均年龄主要为36-40岁(32.5%),其中男性占72.3%,大多数受过高等教育(91.8%),并且是公务员(83.4%)。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 尽管 HBV 疫苗接种 启动和知识水平较高,但 疫苗 完成方面仍然存在巨大差距。该研究强调,81.6% 的受访者表示愿意完成 疫苗接种,这表明如果障碍得到解决,就有可能取得进步。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 解决财务、信息和获取相关障碍对于提高尼日利亚成年人的 疫苗接种 全面覆盖至关重要。这些发现可以为有针对性的干预措施提供信息,以提高医院环境中 HBV 疫苗接种 的完成率。

analysis_zh.main_results: 乙型肝炎总体知晓率较高(95.5%),平均知识得分为12.37 ± 1.42。74.2%的受访者表现出良好的知识,而57.2%的受访者对乙肝预防表现出良好的态度。疫苗接种 的吸收率很高,93.5% 的人报告至少接受了一剂 疫苗,但只有 22.3% 的人完成了推荐的三剂时间表。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 尽管 HBV 疫苗接种 启动和知识水平较高,但 疫苗 完成方面仍然存在巨大差距。该研究强调,81.6% 的受访者表示愿意完成 疫苗接种,这表明如果障碍得到解决,就有可能取得进步。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 解决财务、信息和获取相关障碍对于提高尼日利亚成年人的 疫苗接种 全面覆盖至关重要。这些发现可以为有针对性的干预措施提供信息,以提高医院环境中 HBV 疫苗接种 的完成率。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在一家三级医院进行的,这可能会限制对其他人群或环境的推广。尽管样本量很大,但由于横截面设计和潜在的自我报告偏差,证据强度适中。

title: Differential Hepatitis B Surface Antigen Glycan Isomer Kinetics Between Tenofovir Alafenamide and Entecavir: Hepatocellular Carcinoma Risk Stratification in Hepatitis B e Antigen‐Positive Patients
abstract: ABSTRACT Nucleos(t)ide analog (NA) therapy suppresses hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA, but residual hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk persists. O‐glycosylated hepatitis B surface antigen glycan isomer (HBsAgGi) uniquely reflects virion burden. We evaluated the impact of tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) versus entecavir (ETV) on 48‐week HBsAgGi kinetics and its utility in stratifying HCC risk in 90 NA‐naïve patients (ETV: 73; TAF: 17). A favourable response was defined as a reduction or maintenance of low HBsAgGi levels. TAF independently predicted a favourable response compared with ETV (penalised odds ratio 3.60, p = 0.030). A significant interaction occurred between HBeAg status and HBsAgGi response in relation to HCC development ( p = 0.038). In HBeAg‐positive patients, a poor response was associated with increased HCC risk (hazard ratio 7.34, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.96–20.35, p = 0.001); however, the exact magnitude warrants cautious interpretation due to wide CIs. This association was absent in HBeAg‐negative cases. Adding HBsAgGi response to the aMAP score improved long‐term HCC prediction exclusively in the HBeAg‐positive cohort. As the assay targets genotype C‐specific O‐glycosylation, the findings cannot be generalised to genotypes A, B, or D. In conclusion, on‐treatment HBsAgGi response is a specific surrogate marker for stratifying residual HCC risk in HBeAg‐positive patients, and TAF is more effective than ETV in inducing these favourable kinetics.

title_zh: 替诺福韦艾拉酚胺和恩替卡韦之间的乙型肝炎表面抗原聚糖异构体动力学差异:乙型肝炎 e 抗原阳性患者的肝细胞癌风险分层
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Nucleos(t)ide analog (NA) therapy suppresses hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA, but residual hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk persists. O‐glycosylated hepatitis B surface antigen glycan isomer (HBsAgGi) uniquely reflects virion burden. We evaluated the impact of tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) versus entecavir (ETV) on 48‐week HBsAgGi kinetics and its utility in stratifying HCC risk in 90 NA‐naïve patients (ETV: 73; TAF: 17). A favourable response was defined as a reduction or maintenance of low HBsAgGi levels. TAF independently predicted a favourable response compared with ETV (penalised odds ratio 3.60, p = 0.030). A significant interaction occurred between HBeAg status and HBsAgGi response in relation to HCC development ( p = 0.038). In HBeAg‐positive patients, a poor response was associated with increased HCC risk (hazard ratio 7.34, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.96–20.35, p = 0.001); however, the exact magnitude warrants cautious interpretation due to wide CIs. This association was absent in HBeAg‐negative cases. Adding HBsAgGi response to the aMAP score improved long‐term HCC prediction exclusively in the HBeAg‐positive cohort. As the assay targets genotype C‐specific O‐glycosylation, the findings cannot be generalised to genotypes A, B, or D. In conclusion, on‐treatment HBsAgGi response is a specific surrogate marker for stratifying residual HCC risk in HBeAg‐positive patients, and TAF is more effective than ETV in inducing these favourable kinetics.

title: The relationship between mutations in reverse transcriptase region of hepatitis B virus and progression of liver disease
abstract: The specific objective of this study was to investigate mutations of Hepatitis B virus (HBV) reverse transcriptase (RT) region in Chinese HBV-infected patients at different stages and their association with the progression of liver disease. HBV RT regions in serum samples were amplified and sequenced from 384 patients with chronic HBV infection, including 100 asymptomatic carriers (ASC), 101 chronic hepatitis B, 96 liver cirrhosis, and 87 hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Further analysis of genotyping and AA substitution within RT was performed by the online HBV genotyping tool and MEGA7.0 software. A logistic regression model was used to explore the relationship between RT mutations and advanced liver disease (ALD). The mutation rate gradually increased from ASC to HCC (P for trend < 0.05). Logistic regression analysis showed that one RT site mutation, rtS106A/C, was significantly associated with the ALD. Multivariate regression analysis confirmed that two RT mutations, rtH55R/Q/K and rtS137T/Q/E, were independent risk factors for HBV-related HCC. The current study reveals that mutations within the RT region might be associated with the progression of HBV-related liver diseases and might serve as predictive biomarkers for patients with HBV infection at high risk of developing HCC.

The study aimed to determine whether mutations in the HBV reverse transcriptase (RT) region are associated with the progression of liver disease in Chinese patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study sequenced HBV RT regions from serum samples of 384 Chinese patients with chronic HBV infection, stratified into four clinical groups: 100 asymptomatic carriers (ASC), 101 with chronic hepatitis B, 96 with liver cirrhosis, and 87 with HCC.
analysis.methods: HBV RT regions were amplified and sequenced, with genotyping and amino acid substitutions analyzed using an online HBV genotyping tool and MEGA7.0 software. Logistic regression models were applied to assess associations between RT mutations and advanced liver disease (ALD), including HCC.
analysis.main_results: The mutation rate in the RT region increased progressively from ASC to HCC (P for trend < 0.05). Logistic regression identified rtS106A/C as significantly associated with ALD, while multivariate analysis confirmed rtH55R/Q/K and rtS137T/Q/E as independent risk factors for HBV-related HCC.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as evidence that specific RT mutations may serve as predictive biomarkers for disease progression in HBV-infected patients. The study highlights novel associations between rtH55R/Q/K and rtS137T/Q/E and HCC risk, suggesting potential utility in risk stratification.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results cautiously suggest that monitoring RT mutations, particularly rtH55R/Q/K and rtS137T/Q/E, could inform surveillance strategies and early intervention for patients at high risk of developing HCC. The findings may also guide future research into therapeutic targets within the RT region.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and the study was conducted in a single region with a specific patient population, which may affect generalizability. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 慢性乙型肝炎 病毒 (HBV) 感染会进展为肝细胞癌 (HCC) 等严重肝脏疾病,但进展的病毒学驱动因素仍不完全清楚。该研究旨在确定 HBV 逆转录酶 (RT) 区域的 突变 是否与中国患者的肝病进展相关。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项横断面研究对 384 名中国慢性 HBV 感染患者的血清样本中的 HBV RT 区域进行了测序,分为四个临床组:100 名无症状携带者 (ASC)、101 名 慢性乙型肝炎、96 名肝硬化患者和 87 名 HCC 患者。
elements_zh.methods: 使用在线 HBV 基因分型工具和 MEGA7.0 软件对 HBV RT 区域进行扩增和测序,并进行基因分型和氨基酸取代分析。应用逻辑回归模型评估 RT 突变 与晚期肝病 (ALD)(包括 HCC)之间的关联。
elements_zh.main_results: RT 区域的 突变 率从 ASC 到 HCC 逐渐增加(趋势 P < 0.05)。Logistic 回归确定 rtS106A/C 与 ALD 显着相关,而多变量分析证实 rtH55R/Q/K 和 rtS137T/Q/E 是 HBV 相关 HCC 的独立危险因素。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为特定 RT 突变 可以作为 HBV 感染患者疾病进展的预测生物标志物的证据。该研究强调了 rtH55R/Q/K 和 rtS137T/Q/E 与 HCC 风险之间的新关联,表明风险分层的潜在实用性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果谨慎地表明,监测 RT 突变,特别是 rtH55R/Q/K 和 rtS137T/Q/E,可以为 监测 策略和对发生 HCC 高风险患者的早期干预提供信息。这些发现还可能指导未来对 RT 区域内治疗靶点的研究。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 横断面设计限制了因果推断,并且该研究是在具有特定患者群体的单一地区进行的,这可能会影响普遍性。由于潜在的未测量的混杂因素和缺乏纵向随访,证据强度中等。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 慢性乙型肝炎 病毒 (HBV) 感染会进展为肝细胞癌 (HCC) 等严重肝脏疾病,但进展的病毒学驱动因素仍不完全清楚。该研究旨在确定 HBV 逆转录酶 (RT) 区域的 突变 是否与中国患者的肝病进展相关。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项横断面研究对 384 名中国慢性 HBV 感染患者的血清样本中的 HBV RT 区域进行了测序,分为四个临床组:100 名无症状携带者 (ASC)、101 名 慢性乙型肝炎、96 名肝硬化患者和 87 名 HCC 患者。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用在线 HBV 基因分型工具和 MEGA7.0 软件对 HBV RT 区域进行扩增和测序,并进行基因分型和氨基酸取代分析。应用逻辑回归模型评估 RT 突变 与晚期肝病 (ALD)(包括 HCC)之间的关联。
analysis_zh.main_results: RT 区域的 突变 率从 ASC 到 HCC 逐渐增加(趋势 P < 0.05)。Logistic 回归确定 rtS106A/C 与 ALD 显着相关,而多变量分析证实 rtH55R/Q/K 和 rtS137T/Q/E 是 HBV 相关 HCC 的独立危险因素。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为特定 RT 突变 可以作为 HBV 感染患者疾病进展的预测生物标志物的证据。该研究强调了 rtH55R/Q/K 和 rtS137T/Q/E 与 HCC 风险之间的新关联,表明风险分层的潜在实用性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果谨慎地表明,监测 RT 突变,特别是 rtH55R/Q/K 和 rtS137T/Q/E,可以为 监测 策略和对发生 HCC 高风险患者的早期干预提供信息。这些发现还可能指导未来对 RT 区域内治疗靶点的研究。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 横断面设计限制了因果推断,并且该研究是在具有特定患者群体的单一地区进行的,这可能会影响普遍性。由于潜在的未测量的混杂因素和缺乏纵向随访,证据强度中等。

title: HBV PreS/S gene mutations in patients with chronic hepatitis B
abstract: Variants in the hepatitis B virus (HBV) PreS/S gene have been suggested to contribute to the development of progressive liver disease. This study aimed to evaluate the association between HBV PreS/S variations and liver histopathology in patients with chronic hepatitis B. A total of 109 patients under clinical follow-up for chronic hepatitis B were included. The HBV PreS/S gene was amplified by PCR and sequenced using the Sanger method. Amino acid substitutions, nonsense mutations, and deletions were analyzed in relation to liver fibrosis stage. Overall, 58 of 389 amino acid sites (14.9%) in the HBV PreS/S gene showed substitutions, with the highest mutation rate observed in the PreS2 region (27.27%). Mutations L54P (PreS1), F130L/S (PreS2), and S207R/N/I/T and I208T (S gene) were significantly more frequent in patients with advanced fibrosis (F ≥ 3) (p < 0.05). Multivariable analysis identified S207R/N/I/T as an independent risk factor for liver fibrosis. Patients with PreS2 mutations had higher fibrosis scores (p < 0.05). The S207R/N/I/T mutation in the C-terminal region of the HBV S protein is independently associated with liver fibrosis, while PreS2 mutations may contribute to fibrosis progression in chronic hepatitis B.

title: Absence of Detectable Anti‐ HDV Antibodies Among HBsAg ‐Positive Blood Donors, HIV ‐Infected Individuals and Patients With Chronic Hepatitis B in Sao Paulo, Brazil: Evaluation Using a Rapid Lateral Flow Assay
abstract: ABSTRACT Hepatitis Delta Virus (HDV) infection in HBV‐infected individuals is associated with severe clinical outcomes, and screening is recommended in HBsAg‐positive patients. We used a rapid lateral flow assay (LFA) to assess anti‐HDV antibodies in Brazil, where HDV is highly endemic in the North, while data from the Southeast, particularly São Paulo, remain limited. We conducted a retrospective cross‐sectional study to assess anti‐HDV antibodies among 46 HBsAg‐positive blood donors at Fundação Pró‐Sangue/Hemocentro de São Paulo, 381 patients with chronic hepatitis B from the Central Laboratory Division of HC‐FMUSP, and 189 individuals from the Hepatology Clinic of HC‐FMUSP (101 HIV‐infected and 88 chronically HBV‐infected). Anti‐HDV antibodies were detected using a validated LFA. Positive controls ( n = 24) included samples previously confirmed by ELISA and/or PCR, predominantly infected with HDV genotypes 3 and 8. Among 443,400 blood donations, 48 (0.01%) were positive for at least two HBV markers; of these, 46 were tested for HDV, and all were anti‐HDV negative. All 381 patients undergoing HBV viral load monitoring were anti‐HDV negative, as were all 189 patients receiving hepatology care, including those with HIV coinfection or advanced liver disease. The LFA correctly identified all control samples positive for both anti‐HDV antibodies and HDV RNA. The absence of detectable anti‐HDV among diverse at‐risk populations in São Paulo is consistent with the low endemicity of HDV infection in southeastern Brazil. These findings, together with the assay's high specificity in HDV RNA‐positive controls, support its potential utility as a screening tool for HDV infection in low‐prevalence settings.

title: Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices Toward Hepatitis B Virus Among Transfusion‐Dependent Thalassemia Patients in Jordan
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) studies provide essential insight into public awareness, perceptions, and behaviors toward health issues. Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains a major public health problem in Jordan. Transfusion‐dependent patients are at higher risk of infection due to frequent exposure to blood products. This study aimed to assess KAP toward HBV among transfusion‐dependent patients in Jordan. Methods A cross‐sectional study was conducted among 407 transfusion‐dependent patients attending hematology clinics in governmental hospitals in Jordan. A validated questionnaire assessed socio‐demographic data and KAP regarding HBV. Knowledge, attitude, and practice were each scored out of their respective items; participants scoring ≥ 75% correct were classified as having good knowledge, positive attitude, or safe practices, respectively. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, chi‐square tests, and logistic regression to determine associations, with p ‐values < 0.05 considered significant. Results Of the 407 participants, 114 (28%) had good knowledge, 170 (41.8%) had positive attitudes, and 156 (38.3%) demonstrated safe practices toward HBV. Key predictors of good knowledge included older age (AOR 3.81, 95% CI 2.09–6.94) and higher education (AOR 3.05, 95% CI 1.80–5.16). Safe practice was significantly associated with family history of HBV infection. Significant associations were found between knowledge scores and educational level, employment status, and history of HBV vaccination ( p < 0.05). Conclusion HBV knowledge, attitudes, and practices among transfusion‐dependent patients in Jordan were suboptimal. These findings highlight the need for targeted health education programs and HBV vaccination campaigns for this high‐risk group.

Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains a major public health problem in Jordan. Transfusion-dependent patients are at higher risk of infection due to frequent exposure to blood products. This study aimed to assess KAP toward HBV among transfusion-dependent patients in Jordan. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 407 transfusion-dependent patients attending hematology clinics in governmental hospitals in Jordan. A validated questionnaire assessed socio-demographic data and KAP regarding HBV. Knowledge, attitude, and practice were each scored out of their respective items; participants scoring ≥ 75% correct were classified as having good knowledge, positive attitude, or safe practices, respectively. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and logistic regression to determine associations, with p-values < 0.05 considered significant. Of the 407 participants, 114 (28%) had good knowledge, 170 (41.8%) had positive attitudes, and 156 (38.3%) demonstrated safe practices toward HBV. Key predictors of good knowledge included older age (AOR 3.81, 95% CI 2.09-6.94) and higher education (AOR 3.05, 95% CI 1.80-5.16). Safe practice was significantly associated with family history of HBV infection. Significant associations were found between knowledge scores and educational level, employment status, and history of HBV vaccination (p < 0.05). HBV knowledge, attitudes, and practices among transfusion-dependent patients in Jordan were suboptimal. These findings highlight the need for targeted health education programs and HBV vaccination campaigns for this high-risk group.

elements_zh.main_results: Of the 407 participants, 114 (28%) had good knowledge, 170 (41.8%) had positive attitudes, and 156 (38.3%) demonstrated safe practices toward HBV; key predictors of good knowledge included older age (AOR 3.81, 95% CI 2.09–6.94) and higher education (AOR 3.05, 95% CI 1.80–5.16).
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解释为表明这一高危人群的乙肝知识、态度和实践欠佳,强调了有针对性的干预措施的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,需要为约旦的输血依赖患者开展有针对性的健康教育计划和 HBV 疫苗接种 运动,以改善预防和控制。

title: METTL14 Downregulation Accelerates HBV‐Related Cirrhosis and Hepatocellular Carcinoma by Promoting Type I Interferon Release via the cGAS–STING Pathway Through m 6 A Modification
abstract: ABSTRACT The pathogenesis of Hepatitis B virus (HBV)‐related cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has not been fully elucidated at present. While METTL14 is crucial in innate immunity, its specific role in HBV‐related liver disease progression is unclear. We analyzed METTL14 expression in patient tissues and bioinformatics datasets. Mouse models of HBV‐related cirrhosis and HCC were established to evaluate liver injury, fibrosis, and tumorigenesis. Mechanistic studies utilized MeRIPqPCR, RIP, and Actinomycin D assays, and hepatocyte‐stellate cell co‐cultures to investigate METTL14's impact on cGAS mRNA stability, the cGAS‐STING pathway, and IFNB1 secretion. METTL14 was downregulated in HBV infection, cirrhosis, and HCC. METTL14 knockdown aggravated liver injury, fibrosis, and tumor formation in mice. Mechanistic studies revealed that METTL14 overexpression in HBV‐infected hepatocytes promoted the degradation of cGAS mRNA by increasing its m6A modification, thereby suppressing the cGAS–STING pathway activation and IFNB1 release. Consequently, METTL14 overexpression inhibited stellate cell activation, which was reversed by cGAS‐STING agonists. Downregulation of METTL14 reduces the degradation of cGAS mRNA through m 6 A modification, facilitates the cGAS–STING pathway activation and IFNB1 release, thereby accelerating HBV‐related cirrhosis and HCC progressions.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of METTL14 in HBV-related cirrhosis and HCC, revealing that METTL14 downregulation accelerates disease progression by promoting type I interferon release via the cGAS-STING pathway through m6A modification. The researchers analyzed METTL14 expression in patient tissues and bioinformatics datasets, established mouse models of HBV-related cirrhosis and HCC, and conducted mechanistic studies using MeRIPqPCR, RIP, and Actinomycin D assays. They found that METTL14 overexpression suppresses the cGAS-STING pathway and IFNB1 release, inhibiting stellate cell activation, while METTL14 knockdown aggravates liver injury, fibrosis, and tumor formation. These findings suggest that targeting METTL14-mediated m6A modification could be a novel therapeutic strategy for HBV-related liver diseases.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)相关肝硬化和肝细胞癌(HCC)的发病机制目前尚未完全阐明。虽然 METTL14 在先天免疫中至关重要,但其在 HBV 相关肝病进展中的具体作用尚不清楚。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 建立了 HBV 相关肝硬化和 HCC 小鼠模型,以评估肝损伤、纤维化和肿瘤发生。我们分析了患者组织和生物信息学数据集中的 METTL14 表达。
elements_zh.methods: 机制研究利用 MeRIPqPCR、RIP 和放线菌素 D 测定以及肝细胞-星状细胞共培养来研究 METTL14 对 cGAS mRNA 稳定性、cGAS-STING 通路和 IFNB1 分泌的影响。
elements_zh.main_results: METTL14 在 HBV 感染、肝硬化和 HCC 中表达下调。METTL14 敲低会加剧小鼠的肝损伤、纤维化和肿瘤形成。机制研究表明,HBV感染的肝细胞中METTL14的过表达通过增加其m6A修饰促进cGAS mRNA的降解,从而抑制cGAS-STING通路的激活和IFNB1的释放。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: METTL14的下调通过m6A修饰减少cGAS mRNA的降解,促进cGAS-STING通路激活和IFNB1释放,从而加速HBV​​相关的肝硬化和HCC进展。因此,METTL14 过表达抑制星状细胞激活,cGAS-STING 激动剂可逆转这种激活。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,针对 cGAS mRNA 的 METTL14 介导的 m6A 修饰可能是一种通过调节 cGAS-STING 通路和 I 型干扰素释放来预防或治疗 HBV 相关肝硬化和 HCC 的新治疗策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究主要使用小鼠模型和体外测定,这可能无法完全概括人类疾病的复杂性。由于机械见解,证据强度中等,但由于缺乏人类干预数据而受到限制。

title: Advances in Viral Markers for Predicting Functional Cure of Chronic Hepatitis B
abstract: ABSTRACT First‐line antiviral therapies for chronic hepatitis B include nucleos(t)ide analogues and pegylated interferon‐α. However, neither therapy can completely eliminate hepatocellular covalently closed circular DNA, making complete cure currently unattainable. Functional cure, primarily defined as sustained hepatitis B surface antigen loss, is the optimal therapeuticgoal for chronic hepatitis B. Although combined or sequential nucleos(t)ide analogues/pegylated interferon‐α regimens improve hepatitis B surface antigen seroclearance rates, only a minority of patients achieve this outcome. Therefore, quantification of hepatitis B virus viral markers using standard clinical assays is essential for predicting functional cure before treatment and during therapeutic monitoring. Early identification of patients likely to achieve hepatitis B surface antigen may help loss improve cure rates and potentially reduce medical costs. This review summarizes recent advances in viral markers for predicting functional cure in chronic hepatitis B, evaluates the predictive performance of individual markers, and provides evidence to optimize clinical treatment strategies.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, specifically chronic hepatitis B, and the use of viral markers to predict a functional cure. The central question is how to optimize clinical treatment strategies for chronic hepatitis B by evaluating the predictive performance of individual viral markers. The review does not report on databases, study counts, pooled estimates, or recommendations.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of recent advances in viral markers for predicting functional cure in chronic hepatitis B. It evaluates the predictive performance of individual markers and provides evidence to optimize clinical treatment strategies. The review does not report on the type of review, databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, selection method, included-study count, meta-analysis, or consensus process.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that functional cure, defined as sustained hepatitis B surface antigen loss, is the optimal therapeutic goal for chronic hepatitis B. It also notes that combined or sequential nucleos(t)ide analogues/pegylated interferon-α regimens improve hepatitis B surface antigen seroclearance rates, but only a minority of patients achieve this outcome. The review does not report on pooled estimates or stable conclusions.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights that neither first-line antiviral therapies nor combined regimens can completely eliminate hepatocellular covalently closed circular DNA, making a complete cure currently unattainable. It also notes that only a minority of patients achieve hepatitis B surface antigen seroclearance. The review does not report on heterogeneity, conflicting findings, weak methods, missing populations or regions, or unresolved mechanisms.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that quantification of hepatitis B virus viral markers using standard clinical assays is essential for predicting functional cure before treatment and during therapeutic monitoring. It also notes that early identification of patients likely to achieve hepatitis B surface antigen loss may help improve cure rates and potentially reduce medical costs. The review does not report on future priorities for research, surveillance, diagnosis, treatment, vaccination, ecology, risk assessment, or policy.

analysis.summary_en: This review article discusses the advances in viral markers for predicting a functional cure in chronic hepatitis B. It highlights the current limitations of antiviral therapies, which cannot completely eliminate hepatocellular covalently closed circular DNA, making a complete cure unattainable. The review emphasizes the importance of functional cure, defined as sustained hepatitis B surface antigen loss, as the optimal therapeutic goal. It evaluates the predictive performance of individual viral markers and suggests that their quantification is essential for predicting functional cure before treatment and during therapeutic monitoring. Early identification of patients likely to achieve hepatitis B surface antigen loss may improve cure rates and reduce medical costs. The review provides evidence to optimize clinical treatment strategies for chronic hepatitis B.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染,特别是 慢性乙型肝炎,以及使用病毒标记来预测 功能性治愈。核心问题是如何通过评估单个病毒标志物的预测性能来优化 慢性乙型肝炎 的临床 治疗 策略。该综述不报告数据库、研究计数、汇总估计或建议。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对用于预测 慢性乙型肝炎 中的 功能性治愈 的病毒标记的最新进展的叙述性综合。它评估单个标志物的预测性能,并为优化临床 治疗 策略提供证据。该综述不报告综述类型、数据库、检索日期、资格标准、选择方法、纳入研究计数、荟萃分析或共识过程。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 综述得出的结论是,功能性治愈(定义为乙型肝炎表面抗原持续丧失)是 慢性乙型肝炎 的最佳治疗目标。它还指出,联合或序贯核苷类似物/聚乙二醇化干扰素-α 方案可提高乙型肝炎表面抗原血清清除率,但只有少数患者达到这一结果。该审查不报告汇总估计或稳定结论。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述强调,一线 抗病毒药物 疗法和联合疗法都无法完全消除肝细胞共价闭合环状 DNA,目前无法实现彻底治愈。它还指出,只有少数患者达到乙型肝炎表面抗原血清清除。该综述不报告异质性、相互矛盾的发现、薄弱的方法、缺失的人群或区域或未解决的机制。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, specifically chronic hepatitis B, and the use of viral markers to predict a functional cure. The central question is how to optimize clinical treatment strategies for chronic hepatitis B by evaluating the predictive performance of individual viral markers. The review does not report on databases, study counts, pooled estimates, or recommendations.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of recent advances in viral markers for predicting functional cure in chronic hepatitis B. It evaluates the predictive performance of individual markers and provides evidence to optimize clinical treatment strategies. The review does not report on the type of review, databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, selection method, included-study count, meta-analysis, or consensus process.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that functional cure, defined as sustained hepatitis B surface antigen loss, is the optimal therapeutic goal for chronic hepatitis B. It also notes that combined or sequential nucleos(t)ide analogues/pegylated interferon-α regimens improve hepatitis B surface antigen seroclearance rates, but only a minority of patients achieve this outcome. The review does not report on pooled estimates or stable conclusions.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights that neither first-line antiviral therapies nor combined regimens can completely eliminate hepatocellular covalently closed circular DNA, making a complete cure currently unattainable. It also notes that only a minority of patients achieve hepatitis B surface antigen seroclearance. The review does not report on heterogeneity, conflicting findings, weak methods, missing populations or regions, or unresolved mechanisms.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that quantification of hepatitis B virus viral markers using standard clinical assays is essential for predicting functional cure before treatment and during therapeutic monitoring. It also notes that early identification of patients likely to achieve hepatitis B surface antigen loss may help improve cure rates and potentially reduce medical costs. The review does not report on future priorities for research, surveillance, diagnosis, treatment, vaccination, ecology, risk assessment, or policy.

title_zh: 预测功能性治愈和慢性乙型肝炎的病毒标记的研究进展
source_body_en: ABSTRACT First‐line antiviral therapies for chronic hepatitis B include nucleos(t)ide analogues and pegylated interferon‐α. However, neither therapy can completely eliminate hepatocellular covalently closed circular DNA, making complete cure currently unattainable. Functional cure, primarily defined as sustained hepatitis B surface antigen loss, is the optimal therapeuticgoal for chronic hepatitis B. Although combined or sequential nucleos(t)ide analogues/pegylated interferon‐α regimens improve hepatitis B surface antigen seroclearance rates, only a minority of patients achieve this outcome. Therefore, quantification of hepatitis B virus viral markers using standard clinical assays is essential for predicting functional cure before treatment and during therapeutic monitoring. Early identification of patients likely to achieve hepatitis B surface antigen may help loss improve cure rates and potentially reduce medical costs. This review summarizes recent advances in viral markers for predicting functional cure in chronic hepatitis B, evaluates the predictive performance of individual markers, and provides evidence to optimize clinical treatment strategies.

title: Therapeutic Potential of the Novel Monoclonal Antibody 7-4G against HBsAg in a Mouse Model of Chronic Hepatitis B Virus Infection
abstract: Abstract Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major global health challenge because current antiviral therapies rarely achieve complete viral clearance. We evaluated the antiviral activity of a newly developed monoclonal antibody, 7-4G mAb, directed against the hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg). The antibody showed specific binding to the p27 component of HBsAg and efficiently removed HBV-related particles from patient serum in vitro. Significant HBV neutralizing activity of 7-4G mAb was observed in primary human hepatocytes and in humanized mouse models. In persistently HBV-infected PXB mice, a single administration of 7-4G mAb, either alone or in combination with another monoclonal antibody, reduced serum HBsAg levels and HBV DNA levels by two orders magnitude for two weeks after the treatment. In half of the treated mice, suppression of both viral markers was maintained through the study period, whereas rebound occurred within three to four weeks in the remaining animals. In addition, 7-4G mAb enhanced the HBV DNA-lowering effect of entecavir, a known anti-HBV drug. These findings support the further development of 7-4G mAb as part of an innovative HBV treatment strategy, addressing limitations of existing therapies and advancing toward a more effective HBV management solution.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现支持进一步开发 7-4G mAb,作为创新 HBV 治疗 策略的一部分,解决现有疗法的局限性,并朝着更有效的 HBV 管理解决方案迈进。

abstract_zh: 摘要 慢性乙型肝炎 病毒 (HBV) 感染仍然是全球主要的健康挑战,因为目前的 慢性乙型肝炎 疗法很少能实现完全病毒清除。我们评估了新开发的单克隆抗体 7-4G mAb 的 抗病毒药物 活性,该抗体针对乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg)。该抗体与 HBsAg 的 p27 成分特异性结合,并在体外有效去除患者血清中的 HBV 相关颗粒。在原代人肝细胞和人源化小鼠模型中观察到 7-4G mAb 具有显着的 HBV 中和活性。在持续感染 HBV 的 PXB 小鼠中,在 治疗 后两周内,单次施用 7-4G mAb(单独或与另一种单克隆抗体组合)可将血清 HBsAg 水平和 HBV DNA 水平降低两个数量级。在一半接受治疗的小鼠中,两种病毒标记物的抑制在整个研究期间得以维持,而其余小鼠则在三到四周内出现反弹。此外,7-4G mAb 增强了恩替卡韦(一种已知的抗 HBV 药物)的 HBV DNA 降低作用。这些发现支持进一步开发 7-4G mAb,作为创新 HBV 治疗 策略的一部分,解决现有疗法的局限性,并朝着更有效的 HBV 管理解决方案迈进。

title: Diminished Hepatitis B Antibody Response in Pediatrics With Type 1 Diabetes; the Need for Revaccination Protocol: A Case-Control Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a significant chronic infection in pediatric patients. Vaccination induces production of anti-Hepatitis B surface antibodies, which serve as markers of protective immunity. Given the long-term risks of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma during adulthood, this study aimed to assess and compare seroprotection between children with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) and nondiabetic participants. METHODS: In this case-control study, 127 children with T1DM and 124 controls, all in a healthy immune state and fully vaccinated against HBV, were recruited from Shiraz University pediatric endocrinology clinics. Exclusion criteria included immunosuppression, incomplete vaccination, or hepatitis history in the child/family. Ethical approval was obtained from Shiraz University of Medical Sciences. Comparisons of sex, age, antibody titers, and diabetes indices used appropriate inferential tests; odds of inadequate antibody titers were assessed by logistic regression. RESULTS: Considering an antibody titer of 10 mIU/mL as adequate, the non-protection rate was 54.3% (95% CI: 45.3%-63.2%) in diabetic individuals and 28.2% (95% CI:20.5%-37.0%) in non-diabetics. In a multivariable model controlling for time from vaccination, time from vaccination (OR = 1.26, 95% CI: 1.06-1.49, p < 0.001), and diabetes status (OR = 2.34, 95% CI: 1.33-4.14, p = 0.002) contributed to inadequate antibody titers. Sex, glycemic control, and disease duration over 1 year had no significant effect. CONCLUSION: Children with type 1 Diabetes Mellitus exhibited lower anti-HBs antibody titers compared to their nondiabetic counterparts, with no association found with sex or glycemic control. The timing of vaccination and diabetes status should be considered when evaluating immune responses to HBV vaccination in children.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在这项病例对照研究中,从设拉子大学儿科内分泌诊所招募了 127 名 T1DM 儿童和 124 名对照儿童,他们均处于健康的免疫状态,并完全接种了 HBV 疫苗。排除标准包括免疫抑制、疫苗接种 不完整或儿童/家庭有肝炎病史。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 与非糖尿病儿童相比,1 型糖尿病儿童表现出较低的抗 HBs 抗体滴度,且与性别或血糖控制没有关联。在儿童中评估 免疫应答 与 HBV 疫苗接种 时,应考虑 免疫应答 的时机和糖尿病状况。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,需要为 1 型糖尿病儿童制定重新接种疫苗方案,以确保充分预防 HBV。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于其依赖抗体滴度作为保护性免疫的标志,并且可能存在混杂因素。由于研究设计和病例对照方法的使用,证据强度适中。

title_zh: 患有 1 型糖尿病的儿科患者乙型肝炎抗体反应减弱;重新接种协议的必要性:病例对照研究。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a significant chronic infection in pediatric patients. Vaccination induces production of anti-Hepatitis B surface antibodies, which serve as markers of protective immunity. Given the long-term risks of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma during adulthood, this study aimed to assess and compare seroprotection between children with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) and nondiabetic participants. METHODS: In this case-control study, 127 children with T1DM and 124 controls, all in a healthy immune state and fully vaccinated against HBV, were recruited from Shiraz University pediatric endocrinology clinics. Exclusion criteria included immunosuppression, incomplete vaccination, or hepatitis history in the child/family. Ethical approval was obtained from Shiraz University of Medical Sciences. Comparisons of sex, age, antibody titers, and diabetes indices used appropriate inferential tests; odds of inadequate antibody titers were assessed by logistic regression. RESULTS: Considering an antibody titer of 10 mIU/mL as adequate, the non-protection rate was 54.3% (95% CI: 45.3%-63.2%) in diabetic individuals and 28.2% (95% CI:20.5%-37.0%) in non-diabetics. In a multivariable model controlling for time from vaccination, time from vaccination (OR = 1.26, 95% CI: 1.06-1.49, p < 0.001), and diabetes status (OR = 2.34, 95% CI: 1.33-4.14, p = 0.002) contributed to inadequate antibody titers. Sex, glycemic control, and disease duration over 1 year had no significant effect. CONCLUSION: Children with type 1 Diabetes Mellitus exhibited lower anti-HBs antibody titers compared to their nondiabetic counterparts, with no association found with sex or glycemic control. The timing of vaccination and diabetes status should be considered when evaluating immune responses to HBV vaccination in children.

title: The immunoecology of occult hepatitis B virus infection: genetic remodeling and the immune-mediated microcosm
abstract: Occult hepatitis B infection (OBI) is characterized by the persistence of replication-competent hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA in the absence of detectable hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg). Although typically clinically silent, OBI remains associated with transfusion-transmitted infection, viral reactivation during immunosuppression, and an increased risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The mechanisms underlying this persistent low-replicative state remain incompletely understood. In this review, we summarize current evidence supporting the concept that OBI is maintained through dynamic interactions among viral genetic adaptation, host genetic and epigenetic regulation, and the intrahepatic immune microenvironment. Building upon these observations, we propose the immune-mediated microcosm as a conceptual framework describing how these processes may interact to sustain long-term immune equilibrium. We further discuss emerging evidence for coordinated viral and host genetic remodeling, immunometabolic regulation, and immune checkpoint signaling, while explicitly distinguishing mechanisms supported by direct evidence in OBI from those inferred from chronic hepatitis B, hepatocellular carcinoma, or experimental models. Finally, we examine the implications of this framework for biomarker discovery, risk stratification, and therapeutic development, while emphasizing the current evidential limitations and the need for direct validation in human OBI. Rather than providing a definitive mechanistic model, this framework is intended to facilitate mechanistic investigation, generate experimentally testable hypotheses, and help identify priorities for future research into OBI pathogenesis.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述重点关注隐匿性 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染 (OBI),其特征是具有复制能力的 HBV DNA 持续存在,但未检测到乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg)。核心问题是通过病毒遗传适应、宿主 遗传和表观遗传调控以及肝内免疫微环境之间的相互作用来了解这种持续低复制状态的机制。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该评论是对 OBI 现有证据的叙述性综合。它不报告具体的数据库、检索日期、资格标准或研究计数。该方法包括根据现有观察提出一个概念框架(免疫介导的微观世界),并将 OBI 中直接证据支持的机制与从相关条件或实验模型推断的机制区分开来。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述得出的结论是,OBI 是通过病毒遗传适应、宿主 遗传和表观遗传调控以及肝内免疫微环境之间的动态相互作用来维持的。它提出免疫介导的微观世界作为一个框架来描述这些过程如何相互作用以维持长期的免疫平衡。达成一致的关键领域包括协调病毒和 宿主 遗传重塑、免疫代谢调节和 OBI 发病机制 中免疫检查点信号传导的作用。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 审查强调,OBI 的潜在机制仍未完全被了解。它强调需要区分 OBI 证据直接支持的机制和从 慢性乙型肝炎、肝细胞癌或实验模型推断的机制。目前的证据局限性包括许多提出的机制缺乏人类 OBI 的直接验证,并且该框架是作为调查的促进者而不是确定的模型提出的。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该框架的意义包括促进 OBI 的生物标志物发现、风险分层和治疗开发。该审查确定了 OBI 发病机制 未来研究的优先事项,强调需要在人类 OBI 中进行直接验证。该框架旨在生成可通过实验检验的假设并指导机制研究,而不是提供明确的指导。

abstract_zh: 隐匿性乙型肝炎感染 (OBI) 的特点是在没有可检测到的乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg) 的情况下,具有复制能力的 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) DNA 持续存在。尽管通常临床上无症状,但 OBI 仍然与输血传播感染、免疫抑制期间病毒再激活以及肝细胞癌 (HCC) 风险增加有关。这种持续的低复制状态背后的机制仍不完全清楚。在这篇综述中,我们总结了支持 OBI 通过病毒遗传适应、宿主 遗传和表观遗传调控以及肝内免疫微环境之间的动态相互作用来维持这一概念的当前证据。基于这些观察,我们提出免疫介导的微观世界作为概念框架,描述这些过程如何相互作用以维持长期免疫平衡。我们进一步讨论了协调病毒和 宿主 遗传重塑、免疫代谢调节和免疫检查点信号传导的新证据,同时明确区分 OBI 中直接证据支持的机制与从 慢性乙型肝炎、肝细胞癌或实验模型推断的机制。最后,我们研究了该框架对生物标志物发现、风险分层和治疗开发的影响,同时强调了当前证据的局限性以及在人类 OBI 中直接验证的需要。该框架不是提供明确的机制模型,而是旨在促进机制研究、生成可通过实验检验的假设,并帮助确定 OBI 发病机制 未来研究的优先事项。

title: Trends in Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and HIV Seroprevalence in the Netherlands: Insights From Two Decades of Nationwide PIENTER Serosurveys.
abstract: Hepatitis B (HBV), hepatitis C (HCV), and HIV remain public health challenges despite effective treatments and preventive options. Infections are often asymptomatic, leading to undiagnosed cases, onward transmission, and preventable morbidity and mortality. In the Netherlands, disease burden is concentrated in specific populations, with many undetected infections. We estimated HBV, HCV, and HIV seroprevalence, identified determinants, and assessed trends over 20 years using data from 14,444 participants aged 15-79 years from three nationwide cross-sectional serosurveys (PIENTER: 1995-1996, 2006-2007, and 2016-2017). Participants completed questionnaires on demographics, behaviour, and socio-economic factors, and serum samples were tested for HBV and HCV in all rounds and HIV in 2017. Seroprevalence estimates were weighted to the Dutch population, trends were analysed using weighted Poisson regression, and determinants were evaluated using multivariable Poisson regression. Weighted HBV seroprevalence remained stable across surveys (3%-5% past or present infection; < 0.4% active infection). HBV prevalence was highest among first-generation migrants, with older age, migration background, and STI history as key determinants. HCV seroprevalence remained low (< 0.4%) and was highest among non-Western migrants. HIV prevalence was 0.1% and highest among non-Western migrants and men who have sex with men. Only 9% of active HBV cases were aware of their status. Overall, HBV, HCV, and HIV seroprevalence remain low in the Netherlands but are concentrated in specific groups with limited awareness. These findings support targeted prevention, screening, and linkage-to-care strategies to achieve the 2030 WHO elimination goals and highlight the importance of continued population-based (sero-)monitoring to guide public health policy.
authors: Christine G J I van Straten
Fiona R M van der Klis
Eline L M Op de Coul

title: A highly sensitive and specific fluorescent immunoassay for hepatitis B envelope antigen detection using AIE-encoded nanobioprobes.
abstract: Developing highly sensitive, efficient, stable, and low-cost viral antigen detection strategies suitable for primary healthcare settings is of great significance for the early diagnosis and treatment of viral infections. Herein, we report a highly efficient fluorescent immunoassay strategy for the detection of hepatitis B envelope antigen (HBeAg) based on aggregation-induced emission (AIE) molecule-encoded fluorescent nanospheres. Three AIE luminogens (TPE-Br4, TPE-O2, and TPE-O3) were encapsulated into carboxyl-functionalized nanospheres via an ultrasonic swelling method, yielding uniform and well-dispersed multicolor fluorescent nanospheres. Among them, the red-emitting nanospheres, exhibiting superior photostability, were selected as signal output units. Anti-hepatitis B envelope antibodies were subsequently conjugated onto their surfaces to construct fluorescent nanobioprobes. By integrating these nanobioprobes with a sandwich-type enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, specific capture and recognition of HBeAg were successfully achieved. The proposed method demonstrated a linear detection range of 0.01-1 ng mL -1 and an ultra-low limit of detection (LOD) of 9 pg mL -1 . In addition, it exhibited excellent specificity and robust anti-interference performance in spiked fresh mouse serum samples. Overall, this work presents a sensitive, convenient, and cost-effective sensing platform for HBeAg detection, showing great potential for rapid and on-site screening of viral antigens in clinical applications.

title_zh: 使用 AIE 编码的纳米生物探针进行乙型肝炎包膜抗原检测的高灵敏度和特异性荧光免疫分析。
source_body_en: Developing highly sensitive, efficient, stable, and low-cost viral antigen detection strategies suitable for primary healthcare settings is of great significance for the early diagnosis and treatment of viral infections. Herein, we report a highly efficient fluorescent immunoassay strategy for the detection of hepatitis B envelope antigen (HBeAg) based on aggregation-induced emission (AIE) molecule-encoded fluorescent nanospheres. Three AIE luminogens (TPE-Br4, TPE-O2, and TPE-O3) were encapsulated into carboxyl-functionalized nanospheres via an ultrasonic swelling method, yielding uniform and well-dispersed multicolor fluorescent nanospheres. Among them, the red-emitting nanospheres, exhibiting superior photostability, were selected as signal output units. Anti-hepatitis B envelope antibodies were subsequently conjugated onto their surfaces to construct fluorescent nanobioprobes. By integrating these nanobioprobes with a sandwich-type enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, specific capture and recognition of HBeAg were successfully achieved. The proposed method demonstrated a linear detection range of 0.01-1 ng mL -1 and an ultra-low limit of detection (LOD) of 9 pg mL -1 . In addition, it exhibited excellent specificity and robust anti-interference performance in spiked fresh mouse serum samples. Overall, this work presents a sensitive, convenient, and cost-effective sensing platform for HBeAg detection, showing great potential for rapid and on-site screening of viral antigens in clinical applications.
abstract_zh: 开发适合基层医疗机构的高灵敏、高效、稳定、低成本的病毒抗原检测策略对于病毒感染的早期诊断和治疗具有重要意义。在此,我们报告了一种基于聚集诱导发射(AIE)分子编码荧光纳米球的高效荧光免疫分析策略,用于检测乙型肝炎包膜抗原(HBeAg)。通过超声溶胀法将三种AIE发光体(TPE-Br4、TPE-O2和TPE-O3)封装到羧基功能化的纳米球中,产生均匀且分散良好的多色荧光纳米球。其中,具有优异光稳定性的发红光纳米球被选为信号输出单元。随后将抗乙型肝炎包膜抗体缀合到其表面以构建荧光纳米生物探针。通过将这些纳米生物探针与夹心型酶联免疫吸附测定相结合,成功实现了 HBeAg 的特异性捕获和识别。该方法的线性检测范围为0.01-1 ng mL -1,超低检测限(LOD)为9 pg mL -1。此外,它在加标的新鲜小鼠血清样品中表现出优异的特异性和强大的抗干扰性能。总体而言,这项工作为 HBeAg 检测提供了一个灵敏、方便且经济高效的传感平台,在临床应用中显示出快速现场筛选病毒抗原的巨大潜力。

title: Exploring the role of the ABO blood group types in hepatitis B virus infection: a systematic review
abstract: Introduction ABO blood groups have been associated with several disorders, including cancer, peptic ulcers, coagulopathy and infections. However, the mechanism of this association is unclear. This review examines the role ABO blood groups play in HBV infection. Methods A systematic search of seven electronic databases was conducted using the Population, Intervention/Exposure, Comparator, Outcome framework, including all studies published between 1974 and 2024. The review is registered in PROSPERO (ID: CRD420251243615). Results Thirty-five articles from seventeen countries across four continents were selected for review. Twelve of these demonstrated significant associations between ABO blood groups and HBV infection, with the majority investigating healthy blood donors. Disease progression to hepatic fibrosis and cirrhosis in individuals with chronic hepatitis B infection was associated with blood groups O and A. Conclusions Variable evidence linking ABO blood groups to HBV highlights the role of other factors. Links between ABO blood groups and HBV genotypes remain unclear.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review investigates whether human ABO blood group types influence susceptibility to or progression of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in humans, focusing on the central question of whether ABO blood group is associated with HBV infection or disease outcomes.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a systematic review registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251243615) that searched seven electronic databases for studies published between 1974 and 2024 using the Population, Intervention/Exposure, Comparator, Outcome framework. Thirty-five articles from seventeen countries across four continents were selected.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Twelve studies reported significant associations between ABO blood groups and HBV infection, with most studies conducted among healthy blood donors. Disease progression to hepatic fibrosis and cirrhosis in chronic hepatitis B was associated with blood groups O and A.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights variable evidence linking ABO blood groups to HBV infection and notes that links between ABO blood groups and HBV genotypes remain unclear. The mechanism underlying any association is not established.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to clarify the biological mechanisms linking ABO blood groups to HBV infection and disease progression, particularly regarding HBV genotypes and long-term outcomes such as fibrosis and cirrhosis.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review examines whether ABO blood group types influence hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection and disease progression in humans. Using a registered PROSPERO protocol, the review searched seven databases for studies from 1974 to 2024 and included 35 articles from 17 countries. Twelve studies reported significant associations between ABO blood groups and HBV infection, predominantly in healthy blood donors. Associations were also noted between blood groups O and A and progression to hepatic fibrosis and cirrhosis in chronic hepatitis B. However, the review emphasizes variable evidence and unresolved questions about mechanisms and links to HBV genotypes. The findings underscore the need for further research to clarify biological pathways and inform risk stratification and clinical management.

title_zh: 探索 ABO 血型在 乙型肝炎病毒 感染中的作用:系统评价
source_body_en: Introduction ABO blood groups have been associated with several disorders, including cancer, peptic ulcers, coagulopathy and infections. However, the mechanism of this association is unclear. This review examines the role ABO blood groups play in HBV infection. Methods A systematic search of seven electronic databases was conducted using the Population, Intervention/Exposure, Comparator, Outcome framework, including all studies published between 1974 and 2024. The review is registered in PROSPERO (ID: CRD420251243615). Results Thirty-five articles from seventeen countries across four continents were selected for review. Disease progression to hepatic fibrosis and cirrhosis in individuals with chronic hepatitis B infection was associated with blood groups O and A. Conclusions Variable evidence linking ABO blood groups to HBV highlights the role of other factors. Links between ABO blood groups and HBV genotypes remain unclear.

title: Primary Intraparotid Lymph Node Kaposi Sarcoma in an HIV-negative Patient with Chronic Hepatitis B Receiving Antiviral Therapy: A Rare Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background : Kaposi sarcoma (KS) is a vascular neoplasm associated with human herpesvirus-8 (HHV-8) and is most commonly encountered in patients with HIV infection or other forms of immunosuppression. Primary involvement of an intraparotid lymph node is exceptionally rare, particularly in HIV-negative individuals. We report an unusual case of isolated intraparotid nodal KS in a patient with chronic hepatitis B receiving antiviral therapy. Case Presentation: A 58-year-old HIV-negative man with chronic hepatitis B receiving antiviral therapy presented with a gradually enlarging left parotid mass of 3–4 months’ duration. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography demonstrated a well-defined enhancing lesion within the superficial lobe of the parotid gland. The patient underwent superficial parotidectomy with preservation of the facial nerve. Histopathological examination, supported by positive HHV-8 immunohistochemistry, confirmed Kaposi sarcoma arising in an intraparotid lymph node. Postoperative whole-body PET/CT, performed on two separate occasions, showed no evidence of residual tumor or systemic disease. Conclusion: This case highlights an exceptionally rare presentation of Kaposi sarcoma as an isolated intraparotid lymph node lesion in an HIV-negative patient with concomitant chronic hepatitis B receiving antiviral therapy. It expands the limited literature on this uncommon entity and emphasizes that Kaposi sarcoma should be considered in the differential diagnosis of atypical parotid masses, even in the absence of HIV infection or disseminated disease.

abstract_zh: 摘要背景:卡波西肉瘤 (KS) 是一种与人疱疹病毒 8 (HHV-8) 相关的血管肿瘤,最常见于 HIV 感染或其他形式的免疫抑制患者。原发性腮腺内淋巴结受累极为罕见,特别是在 HIV 阴性个体中。我们报告了一名接受 抗病毒药物 治疗的 慢性乙型肝炎 患者发生孤立性腮腺内淋巴结 KS 的罕见病例。病例介绍:一名患有 慢性乙型肝炎 的 58 岁 HIV 阴性男性接受 抗病毒药物 治疗,出现左腮腺肿块逐渐增大,持续 3-4 个月。对比增强计算机断层扫描显示腮腺浅叶内有明确的增强病变。患者接受了腮腺浅表切除术,保留了面神经。组织病理学检查,在 HHV-8 免疫组织化学阳性的支持下,证实卡波西肉瘤起源于腮腺内淋巴结。两次独立进行的术后全身 PET/CT 未显示残留肿瘤或全身性疾病的证据。结论:该病例突出显示,在同时接受 抗病毒药物 治疗的 HIV 阴性患者中,卡波西肉瘤表现为孤立性腮腺内淋巴结病变,且同时接受 慢性乙型肝炎 治疗。它扩展了关于这种罕见实体的有限文献,并强调即使在没有 HIV 感染或播散性疾病的情况下,在非典型腮腺肿块的鉴别 诊断 中也应考虑卡波西肉瘤。

title: Factors Associated With Surface Antigen (HBsAg) Clearance in a Spanish Cohort of Chronic Hepatitis B Patients: Influence on the Long-Term Prognosis.
abstract: The objective is to identify factors that contribute to hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) clearance in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) infection in an unselected, long-term follow-up hepatitis B open cohort in southern Spain. A prospective open cohort study of 453 patients with CHB infection was recruited in the Liver Unit of the Internal Department of two hospitals in Málaga (Spain) between 1991 and 2022 to assess the incidence of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) clearance during follow-up, identify factors related to it, and determine the influence that clearance had on the long-term prognosis. The duration of follow-up ranged from 0.5 to 36.08 years. A multivariate Cox regression analysis was conducted to identify factors associated with HBsAg clearance. The impact of clearance on long-term prognosis was evaluated using a combined prognostic end point: need for liver transplantation, liver complications, or liver-related mortality. The construction of time-to-event curves was achieved by employing the Kaplan-Meir method, with subsequent comparison of event occurrence between groups conducted via log-rank test. During the subsequent follow-up period, 96/453 patients (21.2%) lost surface antigen (1.96/100 patients per year). Multivariate Cox regression analysis identified as independent factors associated with HBsAg clearance: age at first assessment over 40 years: HR 2.21 (1.38-3.52); a baseline DNA HBV peak below 3.3log10 (< 2000 IU/mL): HR 3.44 (2.01-5.89); loss of hepatitis B e-antigen (HBeAg) during follow-up: HR 7.23 (3.87-13.50). The incidence of HBsAg clearance was 1.96 cases/100 patient-years. It was more frequent in patients older than 40 years, with baseline DNA-HBV below 3.3 log10 (< 2000 IU/mL), and in chronic HBeAg+ patients who lost HBeAg during follow-up. HBsAg clearance was associated with a better long-term hepatic prognosis.

analysis.summary_en: This prospective cohort study in Spain investigated factors associated with HBsAg clearance in 453 chronic hepatitis B patients over 31 years. Key findings included a 21.2% clearance rate (1.96/100 patient-years), with older age (>40 years), low baseline viral load (<2000 IU/mL), and HBeAg loss as independent predictors. Clearance was linked to improved long-term prognosis, reducing liver-related complications, transplantation needs, and mortality. The study provides valuable insights for CHB management, highlighting the importance of these factors in predicting favorable outcomes.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项前瞻性开放 队列研究 研究于 1991 年至 2022 年间在马拉加(西班牙)两家医院内科肝脏科招募了 453 名 CHB 感染患者,随访时间为 0.5 至 36.08 年。
elements_zh.methods: 进行多变量 Cox 回归分析以确定与 HBsAg 清除率相关的因素,并使用组合预后终点评估清除率对长期预后的影响:需要肝移植、肝脏并发症或肝脏相关的 死亡率。使用 Kaplan-Meir 方法构建时间-事件曲线,并通过对数秩检验进行比较。
elements_zh.main_results: 在随访期间,96/453 名患者 (21.2%) 失去表面抗原(每年 1.96/100 名患者)。与 HBsAg 清除相关的独立因素包括首次评估时年龄超过 40 岁 (HR 2.21)、基线 DNA HBV 低于 3.3 log10 (HR 3.44) 以及随访期间 HBeAg 消失 (HR 7.23)。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为 监测 和 CHB 患者的管理策略提供了信息,强调了监测老年患者、低病毒载量患者和 HBeAg 血清转化以改善长期结果的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 尽管样本量大和长期随访提高了可靠性,但该研究的证据强度中等,受到观察设计和潜在混杂因素的限制。

title: Clinically detected hepatitis B virus reactivation in HBsAg-negative, anti-HBc-positive breast cancer patients receiving systemic therapy without antiviral prophylaxis: a two-centre descriptive cohort and nested case study
abstract: Background Hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation is a recognised complication in HBsAg-negative, anti-HBc-positive patients receiving cytotoxic cancer therapy. Guidelines place anti-HBc-positive patients exposed to anthracyclines in a moderate-risk band warranting on-treatment monitoring or selective prophylaxis, yet real-world data from non-prophylaxis breast cancer practice, where serial HBV DNA surveillance is often incomplete, remain scarce. Methods We retrospectively studied HBsAg-negative, anti-HBc-positive breast cancer patients treated with systemic therapy between 2018 and 2024 at two centres in Turkey, none of whom received antiviral prophylaxis. We extracted demographic, oncological and virological data, including baseline anti-HBs titres and all available HBV DNA and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) results, and we quantified the completeness of virological surveillance. Because on-treatment HBV DNA was tested only when hepatitis was clinically suspected, the outcome captured was clinically detected reactivation; the study therefore describes surveillance quality rather than estimating true incidence. With a single event, analyses were kept descriptive. Results Among 139 patients (mean age 60.1 years), 89.2% were anti-HBs-positive and 65.5% received anthracyclines. Baseline HBV DNA was documented in all patients, but serial on-treatment monitoring was not. One clinically overt reactivation occurred (0.7%; 95% CI 0.02%–3.94%) in an anti-HBs-negative woman receiving doxorubicin–cyclophosphamide, presenting as icteric hepatitis at month 4 and responding to entecavir. Since subclinical events would have escaped detection, this figure is best read as a lower bound rather than a true incidence. Conclusions The single reactivation we detected arose in the patient profile that the guidelines flag as moderate-risk—absent anti-HBs together with anthracycline exposure. These observations are consistent with, but do not establish, a risk-adapted approach, given one event and incomplete surveillance. Prospective studies using standardised serial HBV DNA monitoring are needed to estimate true reactivation incidence in this population.

title_zh: 在未进行 抗病毒药物 预防的情况下接受全身治疗的 HBsAg 阴性、抗 HBc 阳性乳腺癌患者中临床检测到的 乙型肝炎病毒 再激活:两中心描述性 队列研究 和巢式病例研究
source_body_en: Background Hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation is a recognised complication in HBsAg-negative, anti-HBc-positive patients receiving cytotoxic cancer therapy. Guidelines place anti-HBc-positive patients exposed to anthracyclines in a moderate-risk band warranting on-treatment monitoring or selective prophylaxis, yet real-world data from non-prophylaxis breast cancer practice, where serial HBV DNA surveillance is often incomplete, remain scarce. Methods We retrospectively studied HBsAg-negative, anti-HBc-positive breast cancer patients treated with systemic therapy between 2018 and 2024 at two centres in Turkey, none of whom received antiviral prophylaxis. We extracted demographic, oncological and virological data, including baseline anti-HBs titres and all available HBV DNA and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) results, and we quantified the completeness of virological surveillance. Because on-treatment HBV DNA was tested only when hepatitis was clinically suspected, the outcome captured was clinically detected reactivation; the study therefore describes surveillance quality rather than estimating true incidence. With a single event, analyses were kept descriptive. Results Among 139 patients (mean age 60.1 years), 89.2% were anti-HBs-positive and 65.5% received anthracyclines. Baseline HBV DNA was documented in all patients, but serial on-treatment monitoring was not. One clinically overt reactivation occurred (0.7%; 95% CI 0.02%–3.94%) in an anti-HBs-negative woman receiving doxorubicin–cyclophosphamide, presenting as icteric hepatitis at month 4 and responding to entecavir. Since subclinical events would have escaped detection, this figure is best read as a lower bound rather than a true incidence. Conclusions The single reactivation we detected arose in the patient profile that the guidelines flag as moderate-risk—absent anti-HBs together with anthracycline exposure. These observations are consistent with, but do not establish, a risk-adapted approach, given one event and incomplete surveillance. Prospective studies using standardised serial HBV DNA monitoring are needed to estimate true reactivation incidence in this population.

title: The Silent Burden of Hepatitis B-Related Stigma.
abstract: Individuals experiencing stigma related to chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection often experience negative self-beliefs, isolation, discrimination, and reduced willingness to engage with healthcare professionals. We aimed to understand the patient perspective of HBV-related stigma and to summarize the patient experience of stigma in a patient-centric conceptual model. Eligible adult participants with a confirmed diagnosis of chronic HBV infection were recruited from the US, China, and Poland. Qualitative, semi-structured, concept elicitation interviews of approximately 60 min were conducted to explore participants' experiences of stigma. Qualitative analysis of interview data was conducted using Thematic Analysis methods with concepts categorized into domains and pre-determined stigma types. A total of 28 participants were recruited from the US (n = 11), China (n = 11), and Poland (n = 6). Internalized stigma was reported by all participants (n = 28; 100%), social stigma was reported by 79% (n = 22) of participants, and institutional stigma was reported by 57% (n = 16) of participants. Seven domains across condition-specific and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) concepts were identified to create a patient-centric conceptual model of the experience of stigma associated with HBV infection. Each domain was reported by at least half of the participants, with social functioning (n = 28; 100%), emotional wellbeing (n = 27; 96%), and HBV transmission (n = 27; 96%) most frequently reported. Experiences of stigma were highly inter-related. Experiences of HBV-related stigma were highly pervasive, with widespread impact on HRQoL. To address the burden of stigma, reducing internalized stigma would be most impactful as this was the most common and bothersome.

To address the burden of stigma, reducing internalized stigma would be most impactful as this was the most common and bothersome.

title: Chronic hepatitis B in a large private hospital network in Türkiye: Clinical characteristics and electronic health record-data gaps
abstract: BACKGROUND: Türkiye has intermediate hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection prevalence and an additional burden of hepatitis D virus (HDV). Large-scale real-world data describing adults with chronic HBV-infection and the completeness of routinely collected electronic health record (EHR) data for HBV monitoring and surveillance is not well characterized. METHODS: A retrospective, cross-sectional study using EHR data from a multicenter private hospital network, including 18,284 adult patients with chronic HBV infection between 2017 and 2025 was conducted. The primary analysis included 17,927 adults with HBV monoinfection, defined as patients without a recorded ICD-10 B18.0 diagnosis code for chronic HBV with delta agent. We described demographic and clinical characteristics, liver disease outcomes, and the availability and consistency of key EHR variables relevant to HBV care, including ALT, HBV DNA, HBeAg, anti-HDV testing, B18.0 diagnosis coding, and structured treatment documentation. RESULTS: Among adult patients with HBV monoinfection, 60.6% were male and the mean age was 53.5 years (SD 14.5). Cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) were recorded in 11.1% and 3.4% of patients, respectively, and were more common among men and older adults. Baseline ALT values were available for 45.5% of HBV monoinfected patients. Among patients without cirrhosis, HCC, or liver failure, both HBV DNA and HBeAg status were available for 1274 of 15,243 patients. Documented anti-HDV testing was available for 2213 of 18,284 patients (12.1%), while 357 patients (2.0%) had recorded B18.0 diagnosis code; only 76 of these 357 patients also had documented anti-HDV testing in available EHR field. CONCLUSIONS: In this large private-sector EHR cohort of adults with recorded chronic HBV infection, cirrhosis and HCC were common, particularly among older adults and men. The findings should not be interpreted as national HBV prevalence estimates, but they demonstrate the value of private-sector EHR data for characterizing diagnosed HBV care while highlighting gaps in laboratory monitoring, HDV documentation, and treatment data needed to support HBV surveillance and elimination efforts.

title: Association of the STAT3 rs1053004 Polymorphism With Hepatocellular Carcinoma in Iraqi Patients With Hepatitis B.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: HCC is still one of the main causes of cancer-related fatalities despite years of intensive attempts to prevent it. One known risk factor is a persistent hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. Previous studies have indicated a contribution of the STAT3 signaling pathway to carcinogenesis through inflammation mechanisms. In this study, we tried to explore the correlation between STAT3 rs1053004 polymorphism and HCC occurrence in people with HBV infection in Iraq. METHODS: A case-control approach was applied with the inclusion of 80 patients with HCC due to HBV infection, 80 patients with CHB, and 80 healthy controls. The study was based on genotyping of the STAT3 rs1053004 polymorphism by a TaqMan SNP genotyping assay. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was used to assess the genetic association with disease risk, adjusting for potential confounding factors. RESULTS: The three groups under study had significantly different genotype and allele distributions (p < 0.001). The HCC group had more T alleles than the other groups. Additionally, patients with the TT genotype had a greater risk of HCC (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 4.26; 95%confidence interval [CI] = 1.89-9.62; p < 0.001), and this impact was observed in patients with cirrhosis, high serum HBV DNA levels, and negative HBeAg status. CONCLUSION: STAT3 rs1053004 polymorphism plays a significant role in the development of HCC risk in people with HBV infection.

title: Using Inflammation as a Framework to Assess Hepatitis B Vaccine Immunity 2259206
abstract: Abstract Introduction Infection with hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains a major global health concern despite being vaccine-preventable for nearly four decades. Although vaccination has significantly reduced disease burden, a subset of individuals fails to develop adequate protection and are classified as non-responders. Methods A longitudinal study evaluated hepatitis B vaccine responses in individuals with or without prior vaccination. Participants received either a 3-dose alum-adjuvanted or 2-dose CpG-adjuvanted vaccine, with a subset receiving a booster. ELISA analyzed blood samples collected on days 1, 8, and 30 to quantify anti-HBs titers, classified as high (≥50 mIU/mL), moderate (10—50 mIU/mL), or low (≤10 mIU/mL). Antibody avidity was measured using a modified ELISA with a chaotropic agent to assess binding strength. Results Age significantly affected vaccine responses. In the booster group, participants under 50 had higher baseline titers, while in the de novo group, younger individuals showed stronger early responses though final titers were similar across ages. Among hypertensive participants, older adults showed slower but steady antibody increases, surpassing younger participants by week 4. Avidity remained stable across both vaccine groups, indicating that prior vaccination increased antibody quantity but not binding strength, which plateaued early. Conclusion Immune recall among previously vaccinated individuals was variable. Although boosters produced a faster antibody rise, a higher proportion of non-responders suggests that prior vaccination does not always ensure lasting protection. Hypertension also shaped vaccine response: while hypertensive individuals achieved early seroconversion, their antibody levels plateaued at lower magnitudes, suggesting impaired immune sustainment possibly linked to vascular inflammation or endothelial dysfunction.Overall, these findings highlight the need for personalized vaccination strategies for individuals with hypertension or advanced age. Funding Source Research reported in this abstract was supported by the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases of the National Institutes of Health under Award Number AI158617. Additionally, supported by Hevolution/AFAR New Investigator Award Topic Categories Vaccines and Immunotherapy (VAC)

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 尽管 疫苗 可以预防近四十年,但 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染仍然是全球主要的健康问题。尽管 疫苗接种 显着降低了疾病负担,但仍有一部分人未能形成足够的保护,并被归类为无反应者。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项纵向研究评估了先前有或没有 疫苗接种 的个体的乙型肝炎 疫苗 反应。参与者接受了 3 剂明矾佐剂或 2 剂 CpG 佐剂 疫苗,其中一部分接受了加强剂。
elements_zh.methods: ELISA 分析了第 1、8 和 30 天收集的血液样本,以量化抗 HBs 滴度,分为高 (≥50 mIU/mL)、中 (10-50 mIU/mL) 或低 (≤10 mIU/mL)。使用改良的 ELISA 和离液剂来测量抗体亲合力,以评估结合强度。
elements_zh.main_results: 年龄显着影响 疫苗 反应。在加强组中,50 岁以下的参与者具有较高的基线滴度,而在从头组中,较年轻的个体表现出更强的早期反应,尽管不同年龄段的最终滴度相似。在高血压参与者中,老年人表现出较慢但稳定的抗体增加,在第 4 周超过年轻参与者。两个 疫苗 组的亲合力保持稳定,表明先前的 疫苗 增加了抗体数量,但没有增加结合强度,并在早期达到稳定水平。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 先前接种过疫苗的个体的免疫记忆是可变的。尽管加强剂产生了更快的抗体上升,但无反应者比例较高,这表明之前的 疫苗接种 并不总是能确保持久的保护。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 高血压也塑造了 疫苗 反应:虽然高血压个体实现了早期血清转化,但他们的抗体水平稳定在较低水平,表明免疫维持受损可能与血管炎症或内皮功能障碍有关。总体而言,这些发现强调了针对高血压或高龄患者制定个性化 疫苗接种 策略的必要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告具体的局限性或证据的强度。该研究得到了美国国立卫生研究院国家过敏和传染病研究所的支持,奖项编号为 AI158617,并得到了 Hevolution/AFAR 新研究者奖主题类别 疫苗 和免疫治疗 (VAC) 的支持。

title: Divergent hepatitis B neutralizing antibody trajectories after spontaneous control in people with and without HIV
abstract: Abstract People with HIV (PWH) have reduced spontaneous control (SC) of acute hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection and increased risk of HBV reactivation, but whether protective antibodies against hepatitis B surface antigen (anti-HBs) remain functional after SC is unclear. We analyzed longitudinal antibody responses of 136 men in the MACS/WIHS Combined Cohort Study with incident HBV followed by SC (99 people without HIV [PWoH], 37 PWH) at the first visit consistent with SC and approximately 6 and 30 months later. Anti HBs titers increased over 2.5 years after SC in PWoH but not PWH. Similarly, HBV neutralization was higher after SC in PWoH and remained stable, while trending downward in PWH. In contrast, antibodies against core antigen declined similarly in both groups. Unexpectedly, hepatitis B surface antigen–anti-HBs immune complexes (HBsAg ICs) were present in the majority of samples and remained stable over time. These findings support persistent HBsAg production after SC, which leads to increasing functional anti-HBs control in PWoH that is impaired by HIV potentially explaining effects of HIV on recovery and reactivation risk.

title: Impact of a multilevel hospital intervention on hepatitis screening and risk management in neuroinflammatory patients receiving immune therapy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with neuroinflammatory disorders receiving immune therapy are at risk of hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) reactivation, particularly in endemic regions. However, adherence to recommended hepatitis screening prior to immune therapy remains inconsistent in neurological practice. This study evaluated whether a hospital-based intervention could improve hepatitis screening and risk management in this population. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective-prospective cohort study in the neurology departments of a tertiary medical center and a regional hospital in Taiwan. The intervention included clinician education, electronic medical record-based screening alerts, and periodic feedback on screening adherence. Screening uptake, screening timeliness, and clinical management actions were compared between pre-intervention (December 2018-May 2021) and post-intervention (June 2021-November 2023) cohorts. RESULTS: A total of 344 patients receiving immune therapy for neuroinflammatory disorders were included. Pre-immune therapy screening rates improved significantly after the intervention for HBsAg (37.1% to 63.3%), anti-HBc (10.1% to 31.8%), and anti-HCV (34.3% to 59.8%) (all p < 0.001). Overall screening rates, including in-therapy testing, also increased substantially. Time-to-screening analysis demonstrated shorter delays for in-therapy screening after the intervention. Clinical responses following HBV identification-including HBV DNA testing, hepatology referral, and antiviral prophylaxis-were significantly more frequent in the post-intervention period. Improved screening also revealed previously unrecognized HBV carriage and reactivation events. CONCLUSIONS: A structured hospital-based intervention integrating clinician education, electronic reminders, and feedback significantly improved hepatitis screening and downstream clinical management in neuroinflammatory patients receiving immune therapy. These findings support incorporating systematic hepatitis risk assessment into neurological care in HBV/HCV-endemic regions.
