title_zh: 多级医院干预对接受免疫治疗的神经炎症患者的肝炎筛查和风险管理的影响。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Patients with neuroinflammatory disorders receiving immune therapy are at risk of hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) reactivation, particularly in endemic regions. However, adherence to recommended hepatitis screening prior to immune therapy remains inconsistent in neurological practice. This study evaluated whether a hospital-based intervention could improve hepatitis screening and risk management in this population. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective-prospective cohort study in the neurology departments of a tertiary medical center and a regional hospital in Taiwan. The intervention included clinician education, electronic medical record-based screening alerts, and periodic feedback on screening adherence. Screening uptake, screening timeliness, and clinical management actions were compared between pre-intervention (December 2018-May 2021) and post-intervention (June 2021-November 2023) cohorts. RESULTS: A total of 344 patients receiving immune therapy for neuroinflammatory disorders were included. Pre-immune therapy screening rates improved significantly after the intervention for HBsAg (37.1% to 63.3%), anti-HBc (10.1% to 31.8%), and anti-HCV (34.3% to 59.8%) (all p < 0.001). Overall screening rates, including in-therapy testing, also increased substantially. Time-to-screening analysis demonstrated shorter delays for in-therapy screening after the intervention. Clinical responses following HBV identification-including HBV DNA testing, hepatology referral, and antiviral prophylaxis-were significantly more frequent in the post-intervention period. Improved screening also revealed previously unrecognized HBV carriage and reactivation events. CONCLUSIONS: A structured hospital-based intervention integrating clinician education, electronic reminders, and feedback significantly improved hepatitis screening and downstream clinical management in neuroinflammatory patients receiving immune therapy. These findings support incorporating systematic hepatitis risk assessment into neurological care in HBV/HCV-endemic regions.

title: Longitudinal Patterns of Chronic Hepatitis B Care and Treatment Adherence in Australia: A National Linked Data Cohort Study.
abstract: Current uptake of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) treatment and care in Australia is well below target levels, leading to an ongoing burden of preventable liver disease and cancer. Understanding individual-level trajectories of care engagement and variation by sociodemographic factors is essential to guide efforts to improve access to and retention in care. This study analysed records of hepatitis B viral load (VL) testing and antiviral treatment provided through Australia's national health insurance system, which were linked to migration, death, and sociodemographic data from various government datasets. Treatment and VL testing by population group were assessed, and uptake was calculated using modelled estimates of the number living with CHB. VL testing frequency and treatment adherence based on scripts dispensed were also assessed. Of the estimated 219,800 people living with CHB in Australia in 2023, 118,334 (53.8%) received either VL testing or treatment during 2014-2023. Estimated uptake of VL testing and treatment uptake were lower among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people and also varied by region of birth. Of the 81,360 who received any VL testing, only 17,352 (21.3%) received it regularly, while 31,715 (39.0%) had evidence of prior monitoring but no VL testing since 2019. The majority of those who initiated treatment continued therapy and received supply sufficient for adherence. This study shows that substantial gaps exist in CHB care in Australia, particularly in continued monitoring among those not on treatment. Disparities in uptake are evident by priority population. Re-engaging those lost to follow-up should be prioritised.

title_zh: 澳大利亚 慢性乙型肝炎 护理和 治疗 依从性的纵向模式:国家关联数据 队列研究 研究。
source_body_en: Current uptake of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) treatment and care in Australia is well below target levels, leading to an ongoing burden of preventable liver disease and cancer. Understanding individual-level trajectories of care engagement and variation by sociodemographic factors is essential to guide efforts to improve access to and retention in care. This study analysed records of hepatitis B viral load (VL) testing and antiviral treatment provided through Australia's national health insurance system, which were linked to migration, death, and sociodemographic data from various government datasets. Treatment and VL testing by population group were assessed, and uptake was calculated using modelled estimates of the number living with CHB. VL testing frequency and treatment adherence based on scripts dispensed were also assessed. Of the estimated 219,800 people living with CHB in Australia in 2023, 118,334 (53.8%) received either VL testing or treatment during 2014-2023. Estimated uptake of VL testing and treatment uptake were lower among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people and also varied by region of birth. Of the 81,360 who received any VL testing, only 17,352 (21.3%) received it regularly, while 31,715 (39.0%) had evidence of prior monitoring but no VL testing since 2019. The majority of those who initiated treatment continued therapy and received supply sufficient for adherence. This study shows that substantial gaps exist in CHB care in Australia, particularly in continued monitoring among those not on treatment. Disparities in uptake are evident by priority population. Re-engaging those lost to follow-up should be prioritised.

title: Hepatocellular Carcinoma Risk Between Untreated Immune Tolerant Vs. Treated Immune Active Chronic Hepatitis B Patients.
abstract: The risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) between chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients in the untreated immune tolerant (U-IT) vs. treated immune active (T-IA) phases is not clear, and most data are in Asian populations. We aim to evaluate long-term risks of cirrhosis, HCC, and overall mortality between U-IT vs. T-IA CHB patients among a national cohort of U.S. We conducted a propensity score weighted analysis of Veterans with CHB who met criteria for U-IT or T-IA from 1/1/2010 to 12/31/2021 (with follow-up through 12/31/2024). Incidence of cirrhosis, HCC, or death were compared between U-IT and T-IA groups. A total of 591 U-IT and 555 T-IA CHB patients were identified (mean age 56.4-57.5 years, 45%-50% non-Hispanic white, 37%-40% African American, 9%-10% Asian, 25%-29% concurrent diabetes, 35%-39% with FIB-4 > 3.25). Over a median follow up of 6.4 years (IQR 3.0-10.4), incidence of HCC was significantly lower in U-IT patients vs. T-IA patients (0.28 vs. 0.54 per 100 person-years; HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.32-0.83, p = 0.007). However, the risk of cirrhosis or all-cause mortality was similar between both T-IA and U-IT CHB patients. Among a predominantly non-Asian cohort of adults with CHB, we observed that HCC risk was lower in U-IT patients compared to T-IA patients. While this contrasts with some studies in Asian countries, these data do emphasize the importance of prioritizing and ensuring timely therapy for CHB patients in the IA phase. However, routine treatment in IT patients remains controversial and more data are needed to better understand long-term outcomes.

title_zh: 未经治疗的免疫耐受者与免疫耐受者之间的肝细胞癌风险接受治疗的免疫活跃 慢性乙型肝炎 患者。
source_body_en: The risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) between chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients in the untreated immune tolerant (U-IT) vs. treated immune active (T-IA) phases is not clear, and most data are in Asian populations. We aim to evaluate long-term risks of cirrhosis, HCC, and overall mortality between U-IT vs. T-IA CHB patients among a national cohort of U.S. We conducted a propensity score weighted analysis of Veterans with CHB who met criteria for U-IT or T-IA from 1/1/2010 to 12/31/2021 (with follow-up through 12/31/2024). Incidence of cirrhosis, HCC, or death were compared between U-IT and T-IA groups. A total of 591 U-IT and 555 T-IA CHB patients were identified (mean age 56.4-57.5 years, 45%-50% non-Hispanic white, 37%-40% African American, 9%-10% Asian, 25%-29% concurrent diabetes, 35%-39% with FIB-4 > 3.25). Over a median follow up of 6.4 years (IQR 3.0-10.4), incidence of HCC was significantly lower in U-IT patients vs. T-IA patients (0.28 vs. 0.54 per 100 person-years; HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.32-0.83, p = 0.007). However, the risk of cirrhosis or all-cause mortality was similar between both T-IA and U-IT CHB patients. Among a predominantly non-Asian cohort of adults with CHB, we observed that HCC risk was lower in U-IT patients compared to T-IA patients. While this contrasts with some studies in Asian countries, these data do emphasize the importance of prioritizing and ensuring timely therapy for CHB patients in the IA phase. However, routine treatment in IT patients remains controversial and more data are needed to better understand long-term outcomes.

title: Construction and validation of a predictive model for HBsAg loss in chronic hepatitis B patients treated with Peg-IFNα-2b
abstract: Background Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) loss is the ideal treatment endpoint for chronic hepatitis B (CHB). Pegylated interferon alfa-2b (Peg-IFNα-2b) is currently the preferred drug for achieving HBsAg loss, but its efficacy varies significantly among different patients. Methods This multicenter, retrospective real-world study enrolled CHB patients treated with Peg-IFNα-2b for ≥48 weeks. Patients were divided into cured and uncured groups based on week-48 HBsAg status and randomly assigned to training and validation cohorts (7:3). Logistic regression identified independent predictors of HBsAg loss and constructed a predictive model. The model’s discriminative ability, calibration, and clinical applicability were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, calibration curves, Hosmer–Lemeshow test, and decision analysis curve (DCA) analysis. Results Among 859 patients, 133 (15.5%) achieved HBsAg loss at week 48. Multivariate analysis identified combination therapy with traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) (OR = 3.83), lower baseline HBsAg (OR = 0.32), lower baseline aspartate aminotransferase (AST) (OR = 0.97), and entecavir (ETV) regimen (OR = 0.33) as independent predictors. The model demonstrated strong discrimination and calibration performance, with AUCs of 0.884 in the training cohort and 0.866 in the validation cohort. Logit(P)=-0.87-1.12*HBsAg(log10)+1.34*group-0.03*AST-1.1×ETV. Note: group (1=no combination with TCM, 2=combination with TCM), ETV (0=non-ETV antiviral regimen, 1=ETV antiviral regimen). Conclusion The combination of TCM therapy, low baseline HBsAg levels, lower baseline AST levels, and non-ETV antiviral regimens were significant predictors of HBsAg loss at week 48 in CHB patients receiving 48-week Peg-IFNα-2b treatment. The predictive model we developed demonstrated high accuracy and potential clinical utility. Key points This study focused on the establishment and validation of a clinical prediction model for HBsAg loss based on a large two-center cohort including 859 patients with CHB. The model was constructed using rigorous statistical methods and further evaluated through both internal and external validation. The results demonstrated good discrimination, calibration, and clinical net benefit, suggesting that the model may serve as a practical tool to help clinicians estimate the probability of HBsAg loss and facilitate individualized antiviral treatment strategies.

title: Frequency of Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C Infections Among Patients With Chronic Kidney Disease: A Retrospective Data-Based Study From Lahore, Pakistan
abstract: Background and objective Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) and chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections are significant global public health challenges, affecting millions of individuals worldwide and contributing substantially to morbidity and mortality due to chronic liver disease and its complications. In Pakistan, the burden of viral hepatitis remains considerable, with HBV and HCV infections continuing to affect vulnerable populations and placing an additional healthcare burden on patients with chronic diseases, including chronic kidney disease (CKD). This study aimed to determine the frequency of both HBV and HCV infections separately among CKD patients and to evaluate their relationship with demographic and clinical factors in a local Pakistani population. Methods This retrospective data-based study was conducted at Chaudhary Muhammad Akram Teaching and Research Hospital (Lahore, PAK) and included 317 medical records of CKD patients aged ≥18 years who presented to the Department of Medicine and Nephrology for dialysis and ICU admission from January to December 2025. Incomplete medical records, patients with acute kidney injury, and records missing hepatitis serologies were excluded. A structured pro forma was used to extract demographic characteristics, CKD-related variables, and laboratory parameters including HBsAg and anti-HCV antibodies from patient medical records. Data were analyzed using SPSS Statistics version 23 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA). Results Of the 317 CKD patients, 185 (58.4%) were male, and 184 (58.0%) resided in urban areas. Mean CKD duration was 2.9±2.8 years, with 185 (58.4%) having CKD for ≥2 years and 246 (77.6%) with stage 5 CKD. Hypertension was present in 271 (85.5%), diabetes in 171 (53.9%), and cardiovascular disease in 72 (22.7%). History of blood transfusion was reported in 140 (44.2%), while 214 (67.5%) had a history of dialysis. The mean hemoglobin (Hb) was 9.3±1.5 g/dL, with 247 (77.9%) having Hb>8 g/dL. Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) positivity was detected in 13 (4.1%) and anti-HCV in 131 (41.3%). Five (1.5%) had both HBsAg and anti-HCV positivity. Chi-square analysis revealed significantly associated anti-HCV positivity with the male gender (p<0.001), urban residence (p=0.038), CKD duration ≥2 years (p=0.027), advanced CKD stage (p<0.001), cardiovascular disease (p=0.049), blood transfusion history (p<0.001), and dialysis history (p<0.001). Binary logistic regression analysis demonstrated male gender (OR=0.483, 95% CI: 0.277-0.839; p=0.010), urban residence (OR=0.520, 95% CI: 0.305-0.887; p=0.016), positive history of blood transfusion (OR=0.348, 95% CI: 0.183-0.660; p=0.001), and dialysis history (OR=0.211, 95% CI: 0.091-0.488; p<0.001) to be predictors of anti-HCV positivity. Fisher's exact test demonstrated a significant association of HBsAg with the female gender (p=0.047) and diabetes (p<0.001). Regression analysis was not applied for HBsAg due to the limited number of participants with HBV positivity. Conclusion Hepatitis C virus was highly prevalent in CKD patients; HBV remained comparatively uncommon. This emphasizes the need for routine screening among CKD patients, especially those undergoing dialysis or receiving blood transfusions. Strengthening infection-control measures, ensuring safe transfusion practices, promoting HBV vaccination, and providing timely antiviral management may reduce the burden of viral hepatitis and improve clinical outcomes in this high-risk population.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study investigated the frequency of hepatitis B and C infections among 317 chronic kidney disease (CKD) patients in Lahore, Pakistan. The study found that hepatitis C virus (HCV) was highly prevalent, with 41.3% of patients testing positive for anti-HCV antibodies, while hepatitis B virus (HBV) was less common, with only 4.1% testing positive for HBsAg. Significant associations were found between HCV positivity and male gender, urban residence, longer CKD duration, advanced CKD stage, cardiovascular disease, blood transfusion history, and dialysis history. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 慢性乙型肝炎 病毒 (HBV) 和慢性丙型肝炎病毒 (HCV) 感染是全球重大的公共卫生挑战,影响着全世界数百万人,并大大增加了慢性肝病及其并发症导致的发病率和 死亡率。本研究旨在分别确定 CKD 患者中 HBV 和 HCV 感染的频率,并评估其与巴基斯坦当地人口的人口和临床因素的关系。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项基于数据的回顾性研究是在 Chaudhary Muhammad Akram 教学研究医院(拉合尔,PAK)进行的,纳入了 2025 年 1 月至 12 月到医学和肾脏病科进行透析和入住 ICU 的 317 份 18 岁以上 CKD 患者的医疗记录。
elements_zh.methods: 使用结构化形式从患者病历中提取人口特征、CKD 相关变量和实验室参数,包括 HBsAg 和抗 HCV 抗体。使用 SPSS Statistics 版本 23(IBM Corp.,Armonk,NY,USA)分析数据。
elements_zh.main_results: 13 例 (4.1%) 检测出乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg) 阳性,131 例 (41.3%) 检测出抗 HCV 阳性。五人 (1.5%) HBsAg 和抗 HCV 均呈阳性。卡方分析显示,抗-HCV 阳性与男性(p<0.001)、城市居住(p=0.038)、CKD 病程≥2 年(p=0.027)、晚期 CKD 分期(p<0.001)、心血管疾病(p=0.049)、输血史(p<0.001)和透析史(p<0.001)显着相关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 丙型肝炎病毒在 CKD 患者中非常流行;乙型肝炎病毒仍然相对不常见。这强调了对 CKD 患者进行常规筛查的必要性,特别是那些接受透析或接受输血的患者。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 加强感染控制措施、确保安全输血实践、推广 HBV 疫苗接种 并提供及时的 抗病毒药物 管理可能会减轻病毒性肝炎的负担并改善这一高危人群的临床结果。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于 HBV 阳性的参与者数量有限,因此未对 HBsAg 进行回归分析。由于回顾性设计和未完全解决潜在的混杂因素,证据强度中等。

Fisher's exact test demonstrated a significant association of HBsAg with the female gender (p=0.047) and diabetes (p<0.001). Regression analysis was not applied for HBsAg due to the limited number of participants with HBV positivity. Conclusion Hepatitis C virus was highly prevalent in CKD patients; HBV remained comparatively uncommon. This emphasizes the need for routine screening among CKD patients, especially those undergoing dialysis or receiving blood transfusions. Strengthening infection-control measures, ensuring safe transfusion practices, promoting HBV vaccination, and providing timely antiviral management may reduce the burden of viral hepatitis and improve clinical outcomes in this high-risk population.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 慢性乙型肝炎 病毒 (HBV) 和慢性丙型肝炎病毒 (HCV) 感染是全球重大的公共卫生挑战,影响着全世界数百万人,并大大增加了慢性肝病及其并发症导致的发病率和 死亡率。本研究旨在分别确定 CKD 患者中 HBV 和 HCV 感染的频率,并评估其与巴基斯坦当地人口的人口和临床因素的关系。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项基于数据的回顾性研究是在 Chaudhary Muhammad Akram 教学研究医院(拉合尔,PAK)进行的,纳入了 2025 年 1 月至 12 月到医学和肾脏病科进行透析和入住 ICU 的 317 份 18 岁以上 CKD 患者的医疗记录。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用结构化形式从患者病历中提取人口特征、CKD 相关变量和实验室参数,包括 HBsAg 和抗 HCV 抗体。使用 SPSS Statistics 版本 23(IBM Corp.,Armonk,NY,USA)分析数据。
analysis_zh.main_results: 13 例 (4.1%) 检测出乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg) 阳性,131 例 (41.3%) 检测出抗 HCV 阳性。五人 (1.5%) HBsAg 和抗 HCV 均呈阳性。卡方分析显示,抗-HCV 阳性与男性(p<0.001)、城市居住(p=0.038)、CKD 病程≥2 年(p=0.027)、晚期 CKD 分期(p<0.001)、心血管疾病(p=0.049)、输血史(p<0.001)和透析史(p<0.001)显着相关。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 丙型肝炎病毒在 CKD 患者中非常流行;乙型肝炎病毒仍然相对不常见。这强调了对 CKD 患者进行常规筛查的必要性,特别是那些接受透析或接受输血的患者。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 加强感染控制措施、确保安全输血实践、推广 HBV 疫苗接种 并提供及时的 抗病毒药物 管理可能会减轻病毒性肝炎的负担并改善这一高危人群的临床结果。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于 HBV 阳性的参与者数量有限,因此未对 HBsAg 进行回归分析。由于回顾性设计和未完全解决潜在的混杂因素,证据强度中等。

title: High Rates of Advanced Chronic Liver Disease in Patients With Chronic Hepatitis D Virus Infection in Uzbekistan.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is endemic in Uzbekistan. Previous data showed a high prevalence of anti-hepatitis D virus (HDV) antibodies in HBsAg-positive individuals. Limited data are available on disease severity, treatment availability and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) prevalence in patients with chronic HDV infection in Uzbekistan. METHODS: The Scientific Research Institute of Virology (SRIoV) is the leading medical and scientific reference centre for viral hepatitis in Uzbekistan. In this retrospective study, epidemiological, clinical and laboratory data were collected and analysed from all HBsAg-positive patients presenting to the SRIoV between June 2023 and May 2024. Data from HDV-coinfected and HBV-monoinfected patients were compared. RESULTS: Data of 1393 individual patients were included. HDV coinfection was more prevalent than HBV-monoinfection (73.9% [n = 1030/1393]) vs. 26.1% [n = 363/1393]. HDV-infected patients were significantly younger (41.9 vs. 45.4, p upper limit of normal. The HCC detection rate was low in both patient groups due to insufficient screening measures (HDV: n = 7/1030, HBV: n = 11/363). CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort of 1393 individual patients, HDV coinfection exceeds HBV monoinfection in prevalence and disease severity. Most HDV-infected patients present with advanced liver disease and currently lack access to HDV-directed therapy.

title: Precise immunomodulation by mesenchymal stem cells mitigates hepatitis B virus-specific CD8+ T cell-mediated acute liver injury without compromising viral clearance
abstract: Hepatitis B virus-related acute-on-chronic liver failure (HBV-ACLF) is associated with a high mortality rate. Although mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) therapy markedly improves liver function and survival in patients with HBV-ACLF, it remains unclear whether the immunomodulatory effects of MSCs suppress antiviral CD8+ T cell function and trigger HBV reactivation. Here, we developed a novel in vitro HBV-specific CD8+ T cell–mediated acute liver injury organoid model, which was co-cultured with either menstrual blood-derived MSCs (MenSCs) or umbilical cord-derived MSCs (UC-MSCs). We found that both MenSCs and UC-MSCs coordinate liver repair and antiviral immunity through precise immunomodulation, primarily via paracrine signaling. Both MSC types significantly downregulated pro-inflammatory ( IFN-γ , TNF-α , IL-8 , and CXCL10 ) and apoptosis-related genes ( FasL and CASP7 ), while promoting hepatic regeneration through IL-6 and HGF upregulation, without compromising CD8+ T cell-mediated HBV clearance. This study provides critical insights into the safety of MSC therapy for HBV-ACLF.

title: Molecular Basis and Clinical Significance of the High-risk Phenotype of Hepatitis B Virus Genotype C
abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) genotype C is common in East Asia and is associated with poor outcomes, particularly liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Clinically, genotype C infection is generally associated with persistent viral replication, later HBeAg seroconversion, more active hepatic inflammation, and an increased risk of HCC. Current evidence suggests that these features are driven by several key molecular events, including the A1762T/G1764A double mutation in the basal core promoter, the G1896A mutation in the precore region, abnormal hepatitis B virus X protein function, and viral integration. Together, these changes may reshape viral transcription, antigen expression, host immune interactions, and oncogenic signaling, thereby contributing to disease progression and hepatocarcinogenesis. Other factors, such as epigenetic changes, dysregulated DNA damage responses, impaired tumor protein p53 function, and disrupted autophagy, may also be involved, although their exact roles remain unclear. Notably, even after effective viral suppression with potent nucleos(t)ide analogs, patients with genotype C may still have a relatively high residual risk of HCC. This review summarizes the molecular virological features, pathogenic mechanisms, immune dysregulation, and clinical significance of HBV genotype C, and discusses the potential value of genotype information in risk stratification, long-term surveillance, and clinical assessment of chronic hepatitis B.

abstract_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 基因型 C 在东亚很常见,与不良预后相关,特别是肝硬化和肝细胞癌 (HCC)。临床上,C 基因型感染通常与持续的病毒复制、较晚的 HBeAg 血清转换、更活跃的肝脏炎症以及 HCC 风险增加有关。目前的证据表明,这些特征是由几个关键分子事件驱动的,包括基础核心启动子中的 A1762T/G1764A 双 突变、前核心区域中的 G1896A 突变、异常的 乙型肝炎病毒 X 蛋白功能和病毒整合。这些变化共同可能重塑病毒转录、抗原表达、宿主 免疫相互作用和致癌信号传导,从而促进疾病进展和肝癌发生。其他因素,如表观遗传变化、DNA损伤反应失调、肿瘤蛋白p53功能受损和自噬破坏等也可能参与其中,尽管它们的确切作用仍不清楚。值得注意的是,即使在使用有效的核苷(酸)类似物有效抑制病毒后,C 基因型患者仍可能具有相对较高的 HCC 残留风险。本文综述了C型HBV的分子病毒学特征、致病机制、免疫失调和临床意义,并讨论了基因型信息在风险分层、长期监测和慢性乙型肝炎临床评估中的潜在价值。

title: Prevalence, incidence and residual risk of HBV, HCV and HIV in Turkish Red Crescent blood donors: A 9‐year survey initiated with the implementation of nucleic acid testing (2015–2023)
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Nucleic acid testing (NAT) has improved blood safety by shortening the diagnostic window period (WP) for transfusion-transmissible infections. Within the context of a national NAT-based screening programme, this study evaluated temporal trends for hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV) and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) among Turkish Red Crescent blood donors between 2015 and 2023. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 22,494,116 blood donations screened by serology and NAT. Prevalence, incidence and residual risk (RR) were estimated using standard incidence/WP models. Temporal trends were evaluated using linear regression, and NAT yield was assessed cumulatively. RESULTS: The overall confirmed positivity (per 100,000 donors) was 288.5 for HBV, 16.2 for HCV and 14.8 for HIV. HBV and HCV showed significant downward trends (p < 0.01), while HIV rose significantly (p < 0.01). Cumulative NAT yields were 189.35, 2.94 and 2.15 per million donations for HBV, HCV and HIV, respectively. Between 2015 and 2023, the estimated overall RR per million donations declined for HBV (634.79 to 238.34) and HCV (1.69 to 0.99), but rose for HIV (4.08 to 11.40). elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 背景和目的:核酸检测(NAT)通过缩短输血传播感染的诊断窗口期(WP)来提高血液安全性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在基于 NAT 的国家筛查计划的背景下,本研究评估了 2015 年至 2023 年间土耳其红新月会献血者中 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV)、丙型肝炎病毒 (HCV) 和人类免疫缺陷病毒 (HIV) 的时间趋势。
elements_zh.methods: 对血清学和NAT筛查的22,494,116份献血进行回顾性分析。使用标准 发病率/WP 模型估计 发病率、发病率 和残余风险 (RR)。使用线性回归评估时间趋势,并累积评估 NAT 产量。
elements_zh.main_results: 总体确认的 HBV 阳性率(每 100,000 名捐献者)为 288.5,HCV 为 16.2,HIV 为 14.8。HBV 和 HCV 呈显着下降趋势(p < 0.01),而 HIV 则显​​着上升(p < 0.01)。HBV、HCV 和 HIV 的累计 NAT 产量分别为每百万份献血 189.35、2.94 和 2.15。2015 年至 2023 年间,乙肝病毒(634.79 至 238.34)和丙肝病毒(1.69 至 0.99)的每百万次捐赠的估计总体 RR 有所下降,但艾滋病病毒的估计总体 RR 有所上升(4.08 至 11.40)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 虽然基于 NAT 的筛查与 HBV 和 HCV 的 RR 较低且不断下降有关,但 HIV 的上升轨迹令人担忧。这强调需要加强行为筛查和捐助者选择策略以及分子检测,以应对不断上升的艾滋病毒风险。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果证明 NAT 在降低 HBV 和 HCV 残留风险方面的有效性,为血液安全策略提供参考,同时强调需要采取有针对性的干预措施来解决献血者中日益增加的 HIV 风险。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和对残余风险估计数学模型的依赖而受到限制。由于样本量较大,证据强度中等,但由于报告数据仅摘要性质而受到削弱。

title: Resolved HBV infection is an independent risk factor for enhanced systemic inflammatory responses in COVID-19 patients
abstract: Purpose To investigate the systemic inflammatory responses and outcomes in coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) patients with resolved hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection or non-HBV infection. Methods This single-center, retrospective study was conducted in Tongji Hospital of Wuhan, China, from 20 January 2020 to 30 March 2020. A total of 215 COVID-19 cases with available test results were included. Demographic and clinical characteristics, and results of laboratory test results, were collected and analyzed. Results Of the 215 included patients, the numbers of patients with current HBV infection, resolved HBV infection, and non-HBV infection were 15, 134, and 66, respectively. Inflammatory biomarkers, such as C-reactive protein (CRP), procalcitonin (PCT), and ferritin, were significantly elevated in the resolved HBV infection group, as well pro-inflammatory cytokines, including interleukin-6 (IL-6), soluble interleukin-2 receptor (sIL-2R), tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF- α ), and IL-8. Resolved HBV infection was independently associated with elevated proinflammatory cytokines. Patients with resolved HBV infection (59.7%) were more likely to develop into a severe state compared to patients with current HBV infection (46.7%) and non-HBV infection (43.9%). Conclusion Resolved HBV infection is an independent risk factor for patients with COVID-19. COVID-19 patients with resolved HBV infection are more likely to have enhanced systemic inflammatory responses and worse prognoses than those with non-HBV infection.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate systemic inflammatory responses and outcomes in COVID-19 patients with resolved hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection compared to non-HBV infection, addressing a knowledge gap on the impact of resolved HBV on COVID-19 severity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This single-center, retrospective study was conducted at Tongji Hospital in Wuhan, China, from 20 January 2020 to 30 March 2020, involving 215 COVID-19 cases with available test results.
analysis.methods: Demographic and clinical characteristics, along with laboratory test results including inflammatory biomarkers and pro-inflammatory cytokines, were collected and analyzed to compare outcomes across HBV infection groups.
analysis.main_results: Of the 215 patients, 15 had current HBV infection, 134 had resolved HBV infection, and 66 had non-HBV infection; inflammatory biomarkers and pro-inflammatory cytokines were significantly elevated in the resolved HBV group, and 59.7% of these patients developed severe COVID-19 compared to 46.7% and 43.9% in current and non-HBV groups, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted resolved HBV infection as an independent risk factor for enhanced systemic inflammatory responses and worse prognoses in COVID-19 patients, highlighting a novel association between resolved viral infections and COVID-19 severity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings inform surveillance and risk assessment for COVID-19 patients with resolved HBV infection, potentially guiding targeted monitoring and interventions to mitigate severe outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's retrospective design and single-center setting limit generalizability, though the evidence strength is moderate due to the clear association and statistical significance reported.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study investigated the impact of resolved hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection on systemic inflammatory responses and outcomes in 215 COVID-19 patients. Results showed that patients with resolved HBV infection had significantly elevated inflammatory biomarkers (CRP, PCT, ferritin) and pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, sIL-2R, TNF-α, IL-8) compared to those with current or non-HBV infection. Additionally, 59.7% of resolved HBV patients developed severe COVID-19, higher than the 46.7% and 43.9% rates in current and non-HBV groups, respectively. The study concludes that resolved HBV infection is an independent risk factor for enhanced inflammation and worse prognoses in COVID-19, highlighting the need for targeted monitoring in this population.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate systemic inflammatory responses and outcomes in COVID-19 patients with resolved hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection compared to non-HBV infection, addressing a knowledge gap on the impact of resolved HBV on COVID-19 severity.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: This single-center, retrospective study was conducted at Tongji Hospital in Wuhan, China, from 20 January 2020 to 30 March 2020, involving 215 COVID-19 cases with available test results.
elements_en.methods: Demographic and clinical characteristics, along with laboratory test results including inflammatory biomarkers and pro-inflammatory cytokines, were collected and analyzed to compare outcomes across HBV infection groups.
elements_en.main_results: Of the 215 patients, 15 had current HBV infection, 134 had resolved HBV infection, and 66 had non-HBV infection; inflammatory biomarkers and pro-inflammatory cytokines were significantly elevated in the resolved HBV group, and 59.7% of these patients developed severe COVID-19 compared to 46.7% and 43.9% in current and non-HBV groups, respectively.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted resolved HBV infection as an independent risk factor for enhanced systemic inflammatory responses and worse prognoses in COVID-19 patients, highlighting a novel association between resolved viral infections and COVID-19 severity.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings inform surveillance and risk assessment for COVID-19 patients with resolved HBV infection, potentially guiding targeted monitoring and interventions to mitigate severe outcomes.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's retrospective design and single-center setting limit generalizability, though the evidence strength is moderate due to the clear association and statistical significance reported.

title_zh: 乙肝病毒感染缓解是 COVID-19 患者全身炎症反应增强的独立危险因素
source_body_en: Purpose To investigate the systemic inflammatory responses and outcomes in coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) patients with resolved hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection or non-HBV infection. Methods This single-center, retrospective study was conducted in Tongji Hospital of Wuhan, China, from 20 January 2020 to 30 March 2020. A total of 215 COVID-19 cases with available test results were included. Demographic and clinical characteristics, and results of laboratory test results, were collected and analyzed. Results Of the 215 included patients, the numbers of patients with current HBV infection, resolved HBV infection, and non-HBV infection were 15, 134, and 66, respectively. Inflammatory biomarkers, such as C-reactive protein (CRP), procalcitonin (PCT), and ferritin, were significantly elevated in the resolved HBV infection group, as well pro-inflammatory cytokines, including interleukin-6 (IL-6), soluble interleukin-2 receptor (sIL-2R), tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF- α ), and IL-8. Resolved HBV infection was independently associated with elevated proinflammatory cytokines. Patients with resolved HBV infection (59.7%) were more likely to develop into a severe state compared to patients with current HBV infection (46.7%) and non-HBV infection (43.9%). Conclusion Resolved HBV infection is an independent risk factor for patients with COVID-19. COVID-19 patients with resolved HBV infection are more likely to have enhanced systemic inflammatory responses and worse prognoses than those with non-HBV infection.

title: A novel LNP/mRNA-based STING immunotherapy approach for chronic HBV infection 2334947
abstract: Abstract Introduction Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major global health burden. Current antiviral therapies suppress viral replication but fail to eliminate cccDNA or substantially reduce HBsAg, making functional cure rare. Innate immune control of HBV is limited by poor engagement of the STING pathway in hepatocytes due to low endogenous expression and inefficient agonist delivery. We developed a universal STING mimic (uniSTING) delivered via lipid nanoparticles encoding uniSTING mRNA, which drives formation of endomembrane-independent STING polymers and preferential activation of the IRF3/type I interferon axis while minimizing NF-κB signaling. Methods HBV-positive cells were treated with LNP/uniSTING, followed by assessment of type I interferon and interferon-stimulated genes (ISG) induction. In vivo, HBV carrier mice were administered LNP/uniSTING, and serum HBV viremia were monitored alongside HBV-specific innate and adaptive immune responses. Results uniSTING elicited strong IFN-I responses in HBV negative cells. In the HepAD38 cell line where HBV transcription from the integrated HBV genome is suppressed by doxycycline to produce HBV predominantly from HBV cccDNA, uniSTING induced robust IFN-β and ISGs expression, whereas in the Dox- condition, characterized by high-level HBV replication, uniSTING-induced IFN-β and ISG responses were attenuated. In vivo, administration of LNP/uniSTING to naive mice induced robust IFN-β production and ISG expression. In chronic HBV carrier mice, repeated administration of LNP/uniSTING resulted in sustained reductions in serum HBV DNA and HBsAg levels, accompanied by induction of anti-HBs IgG responses. Conclusion These findings demonstrate that uniSTING can break HBV immune tolerance and elicit a functional anti-HBs antibody response in vivo. Collectively, this work highlights uniSTING as a promising immunotherapeutic strategy for chronic HBV infection by simultaneously activating innate antiviral pathways and promoting protective humoral immunity. Funding Source NIH R01 AI181664 Topic Categories Viral Immunology (VIR)

abstract_original: Abstract Introduction Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major global health burden. title: Effect of skin tap technique on pain during hepatitis B vaccination among newborns: a randomized controlled trial
abstract: Background: Pain is all about an unpleasant sensation created by stimuli. Every child has his or her own perception of pain. It is unpleasant sensory and emotional experience associated with actual or potential tissue damage. Mechanical stimulation given by taping can diminish the influence of tiny, pain-carrying fibers. This study aimed to assess the effect of skin tap technique on pain during hepatitis-B vaccination. Methods: A randomized controlled trial was carried out among 60 newborns in postnatal ward. Consecutive sampling technique was used to enroll the newborn who met the inclusion criteria. Data pertaining to newborn and a clinical characteristics birth order, gestation age, birth weight and mode of delivery were collected from medical record. Data regarding assess the level of pain during hepatitis-B vaccination by using the neonatal pain scale were collected from skin tap technique. Data were analyzed using Chi-square test, t-test. Results: The data collected was analyzed by using mean and standard deviation. The study findings high light that among 30 newborns vaccinated with the skin tap technique in the experimental group, the majority of newborns, 20 (66.7%), had mild to moderate pain, and 10 (33.3%) had severe pain. Among 30 newborns vaccinated as a routine manner in the control group, the majority of newborns, 22 (73.3%), had severe pain, and 8 (26.7%) had mild to moderate pain, respectively. The skin tap technique was effective compared to the control group. The pain score was 3.83±1.147 and 5±1.174. Respectively with a statistically significant p=0.000. Conclusions: The skin tap technique was effective in reducing pain during hepatitis-B vaccination among the newborns.

title: Development and validation of a machine learning-derived dual-indicator tool for identification of hepatitis B virus-related pre-acute-on-chronic liver failure
abstract: Background & aims Patients who do not meet the criteria for Acute-on-Chronic Liver Failure (ACLF) at admission still face a high risk of disease progression and mortality. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning-derived clinical tool for the early identification of HBV-pre-ACLF. Methods We analyzed 1,682 patients experiencing acute deterioration of HBV-related chronic liver disease but without ACLF. By random forest and SHAP analysis, we identified key predictors of ACLF onset within a 7-day window. We then validated the diagnostic thresholds in a test cohort of 260 patients. Results Total bilirubin (TBIL) and INR were identified as the most critical predictors of ACLF progression. We established optimal diagnostic thresholds at TBIL ≥131.5 μmol/L and INR ≥1.35. Two sequential criteria were developed: pre-ACLF-O (meeting either threshold) for highly sensitive screening, and pre-ACLF-A (meeting both thresholds) for risk confirmation. In the derivation cohort, pre-ACLF-O achieved 98.3% sensitivity, while pre-ACLF-A predicted a 33.09% positive predictive value. These results were successfully validated in the test cohort, where pre-ACLF-O maintained 100% sensitivity and pre-ACLF-A demonstrated a 37.04% positive predictive value. Conclusions This dual-indicator tool easily and effectively identifies HBV-pre-ACLF. Using these criteria sequentially provides a practical strategy for early risk stratification, allowing clinicians to initiate timely interventions for high-risk patients.

title_zh: 开发和验证机器学习衍生的双指标工具,用于识别 乙型肝炎病毒 相关的慢加急性肝衰竭
source_body_en: Background & aims Patients who do not meet the criteria for Acute-on-Chronic Liver Failure (ACLF) at admission still face a high risk of disease progression and mortality. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning-derived clinical tool for the early identification of HBV-pre-ACLF. Methods We analyzed 1,682 patients experiencing acute deterioration of HBV-related chronic liver disease but without ACLF. By random forest and SHAP analysis, we identified key predictors of ACLF onset within a 7-day window. We then validated the diagnostic thresholds in a test cohort of 260 patients. Results Total bilirubin (TBIL) and INR were identified as the most critical predictors of ACLF progression. We established optimal diagnostic thresholds at TBIL ≥131.5 μmol/L and INR ≥1.35. Two sequential criteria were developed: pre-ACLF-O (meeting either threshold) for highly sensitive screening, and pre-ACLF-A (meeting both thresholds) for risk confirmation. In the derivation cohort, pre-ACLF-O achieved 98.3% sensitivity, while pre-ACLF-A predicted a 33.09% positive predictive value. These results were successfully validated in the test cohort, where pre-ACLF-O maintained 100% sensitivity and pre-ACLF-A demonstrated a 37.04% positive predictive value. Conclusions This dual-indicator tool easily and effectively identifies HBV-pre-ACLF. Using these criteria sequentially provides a practical strategy for early risk stratification, allowing clinicians to initiate timely interventions for high-risk patients.

title: Hubungan Kadar Albumin Plasma pada Penderita TB Mdr dengan Ko-Infeksi Hepatitis B
abstract: ABSTRACT Tuberculosis is a chronic infectious disease caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Resistance of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) germ is caused by spontaneous mutations in the chromosome. The proportion of Mtb germs that have undergone mutation (wild-type resistant mutants) in patients who have never received OAT is very small. TB treatment causes selective inhibition of the Mtb germ population, leading to the killing of sensitive Mtb germs, while the mutant population will reproduce and cause resistance to OAT (acquired resistance). A common co-infection in TB patients is Hepatitis B. Hepatitis B infection is a liver disease that causes inflammation and damage to hepatocytes. Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in tuberculosis patients ranges from 0.5% to 44%. Hypoalbuminemia is often associated with both TB and Hepatitis B. It frequently occurs in hepatitis B due to liver damage caused by hepatitis B virus infection, while in TB, hypoalbuminemia is often linked to malnutrition and poor nutritional intake in TB patients. This hypothesis aligns with the patient's current condition, where the patient is diagnosed with hepatitis B confirmed by laboratory results showing HBsAg values 1000. Additionally, the patient also suffers from MDR TB with poor nutritional intake, as evidenced by the patient's BMI of only 19.53. Keywords: Hepatitis B, Hypoalbuminemia, Co-infection, Multi-drug resistant, Tuberculosis, Multi-Drug Resistant. ABSTRAK Tuberkulosis ada suatu penyakit kronik menular yang disebabkan oleh bakteri Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Resistansi kuman Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) disebabkan oleh mutasi spontan pada kromosom. Proporsi kuman Mtb yang sudah mengalami mutasi (wild-type resistant mutants) pada pasien yang tidak pernah mendapatkan OAT sangat sedikit. Pengobatan TB menyebabkan hambatan selektif pada populasi kuman Mtb sehingga kuman Mtb sensitif dibunuh, sementara populasi mutan akan bereproduksi dan menyebabkan terjadinya resistansi terhadap OAT (resistansi didapat). Ko-infeksi yang sering terjadi pada pasien TB adalah Hepatitis B. Infeksi hepatitis B adalah penyakit hati yang menyebabkan peradangan dan kerusakan hepatosit. Infeksi virus hepatitis B (HBV) kronis pada pasien tuberkulosis berkisar antara 0,5% hingga 44%. Hipoalbuminemia sering dikaitkan dengan penyakit TB maupun Hepatitis B. Pada hepatitis B sering terjadi dikarenakan adanya kerusakan hati yang disebabkan oleh infeksi virus hepatitis B, sedangkan pada TB sering terjadi hipoalbumin dikaitkan dengan malnutrisi dan kurangnya asupan gizi pada pasien TB. Hipotesis ini sesuai dengan kondisi pasien pada saat ini, dimana pasien didiagnosis hepatitis B yang ditegakkan dengan hasil pemeriksaan labortarorium dimana nilai HBsAg 1000, selain itu pasien juga menderita TB MDR dengan asupan gizi yang buruk, dimana dapat dilihat BMI pasien hanya 19.53. Kata Kunci: Hepatitis B, Hipoalbuminemia, Ko-Infeksi, Multi Drug Resistant, Tuberkulosis, Multi Drug Resistant.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the relationship between plasma albumin levels in patients with multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR TB) and co-infection with hepatitis B.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study examined a patient diagnosed with hepatitis B confirmed by laboratory results showing HBsAg values of 1000 and MDR TB with poor nutritional intake, evidenced by a BMI of only 19.53.
analysis.methods: The study hypothesized that hypoalbuminemia is associated with both TB and hepatitis B, with hepatitis B causing liver damage and TB linked to malnutrition and poor nutritional intake.
analysis.main_results: The patient's condition aligned with the hypothesis, showing hepatitis B confirmed by laboratory results and MDR TB with poor nutritional intake, evidenced by a BMI of 19.53.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that hypoalbuminemia in co-infected patients may result from both liver damage due to hepatitis B and malnutrition associated with TB.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study highlights the importance of monitoring albumin levels in MDR TB patients with hepatitis B co-infection to assess nutritional status and liver function.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is based on a single case study, limiting generalizability, but provides specific insights into the relationship between hypoalbuminemia, TB, and hepatitis B co-infection.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the relationship between plasma albumin levels in patients with multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR TB) and co-infection with hepatitis B. The case study describes a patient with hepatitis B confirmed by laboratory results (HBsAg 1000) and MDR TB with poor nutritional intake (BMI 19.53). The hypothesis suggests hypoalbuminemia in these patients results from both liver damage due to hepatitis B and malnutrition associated with TB. The findings highlight the importance of monitoring albumin levels in co-infected patients to assess nutritional status and liver function. However, the evidence is limited to a single case study, reducing generalizability.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在探讨耐多药结核病(MDR TB)患者血浆白蛋白水平与合并感染乙型肝炎之间的关系。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究检查了一名被诊断为乙型肝炎的患者,实验室结果显示 HBsAg 值为 1000,且患有耐多药结核病,且营养摄入不足,BMI 仅 19.53。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究假设低白蛋白血症与结核病和乙型肝炎有关,乙型肝炎会导致肝损伤,而结核病则与营养不良和营养摄入不足有关。
elements_zh.main_results: 患者的病情与假设相符,实验室结果证实患有乙型肝炎,并且患有耐多药结核病且营养摄入不足,BMI 为 19.53。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,合并感染患者的低白蛋白血症可能是由乙型肝炎引起的肝损伤和结核病相关营养不良造成的。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究强调了监测合并乙型肝炎的耐多药结核病患者的白蛋白水平对于评估营养状况和肝功能的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该证据基于单个病例研究,限制了普遍性,但提供了对低白蛋白血症、结核病和乙型肝炎合并感染之间关系的具体见解。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the relationship between plasma albumin levels in patients with multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR TB) and co-infection with hepatitis B.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study examined a patient diagnosed with hepatitis B confirmed by laboratory results showing HBsAg values of 1000 and MDR TB with poor nutritional intake, evidenced by a BMI of only 19.53.
analysis_en.methods: The study hypothesized that hypoalbuminemia is associated with both TB and hepatitis B, with hepatitis B causing liver damage and TB linked to malnutrition and poor nutritional intake.
analysis_en.main_results: The patient's condition aligned with the hypothesis, showing hepatitis B confirmed by laboratory results and MDR TB with poor nutritional intake, evidenced by a BMI of 19.53.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that hypoalbuminemia in co-infected patients may result from both liver damage due to hepatitis B and malnutrition associated with TB.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study highlights the importance of monitoring albumin levels in MDR TB patients with hepatitis B co-infection to assess nutritional status and liver function.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is based on a single case study, limiting generalizability, but provides specific insights into the relationship between hypoalbuminemia, TB, and hepatitis B co-infection.

title_zh: Hubungan Kadar 白蛋白 Plasma pada Penderita TB Mdr dengan Ko-Infeksi 乙型肝炎
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Tuberculosis is a chronic infectious disease caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Resistance of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) germ is caused by spontaneous mutations in the chromosome. The proportion of Mtb germs that have undergone mutation (wild-type resistant mutants) in patients who have never received OAT is very small. TB treatment causes selective inhibition of the Mtb germ population, leading to the killing of sensitive Mtb germs, while the mutant population will reproduce and cause resistance to OAT (acquired resistance). A common co-infection in TB patients is Hepatitis B. Hepatitis B infection is a liver disease that causes inflammation and damage to hepatocytes. Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in tuberculosis patients ranges from 0.5% to 44%. Hypoalbuminemia is often associated with both TB and Hepatitis B. It frequently occurs in hepatitis B due to liver damage caused by hepatitis B virus infection, while in TB, hypoalbuminemia is often linked to malnutrition and poor nutritional intake in TB patients. This hypothesis aligns with the patient's current condition, where the patient is diagnosed with hepatitis B confirmed by laboratory results showing HBsAg values 1000. Additionally, the patient also suffers from MDR TB with poor nutritional intake, as evidenced by the patient's BMI of only 19.53. Keywords: Hepatitis B, Hypoalbuminemia, Co-infection, Multi-drug resistant, Tuberculosis, Multi-Drug Resistant. ABSTRAK Tuberkulosis ada suatu penyakit kronik menular yang disebabkan oleh bakteri Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Resistansi kuman Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) disebabkan oleh mutasi spontan pada kromosom. Proporsi kuman Mtb yang sudah mengalami mutasi (wild-type resistant mutants) pada pasien yang tidak pernah mendapatkan OAT sangat sedikit. Pengobatan TB menyebabkan hambatan selektif pada populasi kuman Mtb sehingga kuman Mtb sensitif dibunuh, sementara populasi mutan akan bereproduksi dan menyebabkan terjadinya resistansi terhadap OAT (resistansi didapat). Ko-infeksi yang sering terjadi pada pasien TB adalah Hepatitis B. Infeksi hepatitis B adalah penyakit hati yang menyebabkan peradangan dan kerusakan hepatosit. Infeksi virus hepatitis B (HBV) kronis pada pasien tuberkulosis berkisar antara 0,5% hingga 44%. Hipoalbuminemia sering dikaitkan dengan penyakit TB maupun Hepatitis B. Pada hepatitis B sering terjadi dikarenakan adanya kerusakan hati yang disebabkan oleh infeksi virus hepatitis B, sedangkan pada TB sering terjadi hipoalbumin dikaitkan dengan malnutrisi dan kurangnya asupan gizi pada pasien TB. Hipotesis ini sesuai dengan kondisi pasien pada saat ini, dimana pasien didiagnosis hepatitis B yang ditegakkan dengan hasil pemeriksaan labortarorium dimana nilai HBsAg 1000, selain itu pasien juga menderita TB MDR dengan asupan gizi yang buruk, dimana dapat dilihat BMI pasien hanya 19.53. title: Development of T-cell-based immunotherapy against chronic Hepatitis B infection 2309924
abstract: Abstract Introduction Even though T cells are known to be essential for Hepatitis B virus (HBV) clearance, there is currently no FDA-approved immunotherapy against chronic HBV infection, one of the major global causes of liver cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). We aimed to characterize and test HBV-specific T cell receptors (TCRs) in a rhesus macaque (RMs) model of acute HBV clearance. Methods We analyzed HBV-specific T cell responses using non-parenchymal liver cells from RMs that cleared HBV by enzyme-linked immunospot and intracellular cytokine staining (ICS). We live-sorted activated HBV-specific CD8+ T cells from an animal with the strongest response using the TNF-α processing inhibitor (TAPI-0) and analyzed their transcriptional profile as well as T cell receptors (TCRs) via single-cell RNAseq. We used the retroviral method of expressing the α and β TCR chains from the top 8 most enriched TCRs in naive CD8+ T cells to confirm their specificity, map the minimal epitope, and identify MHC restriction. Results We identified three animals with strong CD8+ T cell responses against the same HBV surface 15-mer. The transcriptional profile showed that the responding CD8+ T cells primarily expressed αβ TCR chains and were highly activated. Using ICS, we confirmed the anti-viral activity of 3 TCRs. Peptide dilution experiments using T cells transduced with these TCRs showed that the immunogenic peptide is FLLTRILTI, which is known to be presented by HLA-A*02 in humans. We also determined that in RMs the restricting allele for this peptide is Mamu-B*031:01:01. Conclusion One of the main challenges in developing immunotherapy against chronic HBV infection is a lack of pre-clinical animal models. We show that RMs can be used to identify HBV-specific CD8+ T cell responses. Future directions include developing MHC-peptide tetramers to detect and elucidate HBV-specific T cell responses, identifying HBV-specific TCRs against other HBV proteins, and testing T-cell-based immunotherapy efficiency and safety. Funding Source n/a Topic Categories Vaccines and Immunotherapy (VAC)

title_zh: 针对 慢性乙型肝炎 感染的基于 T 细胞的免疫疗法的开发 2309924
source_body_en: Abstract Introduction Even though T cells are known to be essential for Hepatitis B virus (HBV) clearance, there is currently no FDA-approved immunotherapy against chronic HBV infection, one of the major global causes of liver cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). We aimed to characterize and test HBV-specific T cell receptors (TCRs) in a rhesus macaque (RMs) model of acute HBV clearance. Methods We analyzed HBV-specific T cell responses using non-parenchymal liver cells from RMs that cleared HBV by enzyme-linked immunospot and intracellular cytokine staining (ICS). We live-sorted activated HBV-specific CD8+ T cells from an animal with the strongest response using the TNF-α processing inhibitor (TAPI-0) and analyzed their transcriptional profile as well as T cell receptors (TCRs) via single-cell RNAseq. We used the retroviral method of expressing the α and β TCR chains from the top 8 most enriched TCRs in naive CD8+ T cells to confirm their specificity, map the minimal epitope, and identify MHC restriction. Results We identified three animals with strong CD8+ T cell responses against the same HBV surface 15-mer. The transcriptional profile showed that the responding CD8+ T cells primarily expressed αβ TCR chains and were highly activated. Using ICS, we confirmed the anti-viral activity of 3 TCRs. Peptide dilution experiments using T cells transduced with these TCRs showed that the immunogenic peptide is FLLTRILTI, which is known to be presented by HLA-A*02 in humans. We also determined that in RMs the restricting allele for this peptide is Mamu-B*031:01:01. Conclusion One of the main challenges in developing immunotherapy against chronic HBV infection is a lack of pre-clinical animal models. We show that RMs can be used to identify HBV-specific CD8+ T cell responses. Future directions include developing MHC-peptide tetramers to detect and elucidate HBV-specific T cell responses, identifying HBV-specific TCRs against other HBV proteins, and testing T-cell-based immunotherapy efficiency and safety. title: ddOTs: A multiplexed quantitative ddPCR approach for resolving overlapping hepatitis B virus transcripts to decipher cccDNA-driven transcription
abstract: Chronic hepatitis B virus infection persists as a global health crisis, driving life-threatening liver pathologies such as hepatocellular carcinoma. Central to HBV’s resilience is the covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA), a viral minichromosome that orchestrates viral transcription and sustains infection. Dissecting cccDNA-driven transcription remains a formidable challenge due to the dense overlap of viral open reading frames, which generates RNA transcripts with shared sequences, complicating precise quantification and hindering efforts to unravel HBV’s transcriptional regulation. To address this bottleneck, we developed a multiplexed assay named ddPCR for Overlapping Transcripts (ddOTs) capable of simultaneously quantifying all major HBV RNA species, including splice variants, with unprecedented specificity and sensitivity. This method overcomes current limitations by leveraging the high-resolution power of ddPCR to deconvolute overlapping transcripts, enabling direct interrogation of individual promoter/enhancer activities and RNA stability. By offering a cost-effective, scalable solution for precise RNA profiling in rare biological samples, this breakthrough tool unlocks new avenues for exploring cccDNA biology and accelerating antiviral drug development.

title_zh: ddOTs:一种多重定量 ddPCR 方法,用于解析重叠的 乙型肝炎病毒 转录本以破译 共价闭合环状DNA 驱动的转录
source_body_en: Chronic hepatitis B virus infection persists as a global health crisis, driving life-threatening liver pathologies such as hepatocellular carcinoma. Central to HBV’s resilience is the covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA), a viral minichromosome that orchestrates viral transcription and sustains infection. Dissecting cccDNA-driven transcription remains a formidable challenge due to the dense overlap of viral open reading frames, which generates RNA transcripts with shared sequences, complicating precise quantification and hindering efforts to unravel HBV’s transcriptional regulation. To address this bottleneck, we developed a multiplexed assay named ddPCR for Overlapping Transcripts (ddOTs) capable of simultaneously quantifying all major HBV RNA species, including splice variants, with unprecedented specificity and sensitivity. This method overcomes current limitations by leveraging the high-resolution power of ddPCR to deconvolute overlapping transcripts, enabling direct interrogation of individual promoter/enhancer activities and RNA stability. By offering a cost-effective, scalable solution for precise RNA profiling in rare biological samples, this breakthrough tool unlocks new avenues for exploring cccDNA biology and accelerating antiviral drug development.
abstract_zh: 慢性乙型肝炎 病毒感染持续成为全球健康危机,导致肝细胞癌等危及生命的肝脏病变。HBV 恢复能力的核心是共价闭合环状 DNA (共价闭合环状DNA),这是一种病毒微型染色体,可以协调病毒转录并维持感染。由于病毒开放阅读框的密集重叠,剖析 共价闭合环状DNA 驱动的转录仍然是一项艰巨的挑战,这会产生具有共享序列的 RNA 转录本,使精确定量变得复杂,并阻碍了阐明 HBV 转录调控的努力。为了解决这个瓶颈,我们开发了一种名为 ddPCR for Overlapping Transcripts (ddOTs) 的多重检测,能够同时定量所有主要 HBV RNA 种类,包括剪接变体,具有前所未有的特异性和灵敏度。该方法通过利用 ddPCR 的高分辨率能力来解卷积重叠转录本,从而克服了当前的局限性,从而能够直接询问单个启动子/增强子活性和 RNA 稳定性。通过为稀有生物样品中的精确 RNA 分析提供经济高效、可扩展的解决方案,这一突破性工具为探索 共价闭合环状DNA 生物学和加速 抗病毒药物 药物开发开辟了新途径。

title: lncRNA ZNF667-AS1 suppresses hepatitis B virus-related hepatocellular carcinoma by regulating miR-210-3p to upregulate CPEB2
abstract: To explore the biological functions, clinical significance, and regulatory mechanism of long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) ZNF667-AS1 in hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). One hundred and seven patients with HBV-related HCC, one hundred and five patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and one hundred and five healthy controls were enrolled in this study. Real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) was used to detect the expression levels of ZNF667-AS1, miR-210-3p, CPEB2. The association between ZNF667-AS1 expression and clinical characteristics of patients were analyzed, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to evaluate its diagnostic value. Bioinformatics prediction and dual-luciferase reporter assays were conducted to verify the targeted associations between ZNF667-AS1 and miR-210-3p, as well as between miR-210-3p and CPEB2. Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) and Transwell assays were applied to assess the biological functions of HCC cells after cell transfection. The expression levels of ZNF667-AS1 and CPEB2 were significantly downregulated in tissue samples from patients with HBV-related HCC and in HBV-associated HCC cell lines. ROC curve analysis showed the area under the curve (AUC) of ZNF667-AS1 for diagnosing HBV-related HCC from CHB reached 0.841. miR-210-3p was validated as a direct target of ZNF667-AS1, and a significant negative correlation was observed between their expression levels. Overexpression of ZNF667-AS1 inhibited the proliferation, migration, and invasion of HCC cells, whereas this inhibitory effect was reversed by transfection with miR-210-3p mimic. LncRNA ZNF667-AS1 is downregulated in HBV-related HCC and exerts in vitro tumor‐suppressive effects by targeting miR-210-3p to upregulate CPEB2 expression, thus providing a potential auxiliary biomarker for HBV-related HCC diagnosis and a novel regulatory axis for understanding disease pathogenesis.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study enrolled 107 patients with HBV-related HCC, 105 patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB), and 105 healthy controls to investigate lncRNA ZNF667-AS1 expression and its clinical associations.
analysis.methods: RT-qPCR was used to quantify ZNF667-AS1, miR-210-3p, and CPEB2 expression levels. analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the role of lncRNA ZNF667-AS1 in HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) by enrolling 107 HBV-HCC patients, 105 chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients, and 105 healthy controls. Using RT-qPCR, dual-luciferase reporter assays, and functional cell assays, the authors demonstrated that ZNF667-AS1 is downregulated in HBV-HCC tissues and cell lines and exerts tumor-suppressive effects by targeting miR-210-3p to upregulate CPEB2. ROC analysis showed an AUC of 0.841 for ZNF667-AS1 in distinguishing HBV-HCC from CHB, supporting its potential as an auxiliary diagnostic biomarker. The study interprets ZNF667-AS1 as a novel regulatory axis in HBV-HCC pathogenesis and suggests therapeutic implications, though limitations include in vitro focus and single-center design, warranting moderate confidence.

title_zh: lncRNA ZNF667-AS1通过调节miR-210-3p上调CPEB2抑制乙型肝炎病毒相关肝细胞癌
source_body_en: To explore the biological functions, clinical significance, and regulatory mechanism of long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) ZNF667-AS1 in hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). One hundred and seven patients with HBV-related HCC, one hundred and five patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and one hundred and five healthy controls were enrolled in this study. Real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) was used to detect the expression levels of ZNF667-AS1, miR-210-3p, CPEB2. The association between ZNF667-AS1 expression and clinical characteristics of patients were analyzed, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to evaluate its diagnostic value. Bioinformatics prediction and dual-luciferase reporter assays were conducted to verify the targeted associations between ZNF667-AS1 and miR-210-3p, as well as between miR-210-3p and CPEB2. Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) and Transwell assays were applied to assess the biological functions of HCC cells after cell transfection. The expression levels of ZNF667-AS1 and CPEB2 were significantly downregulated in tissue samples from patients with HBV-related HCC and in HBV-associated HCC cell lines. ROC curve analysis showed the area under the curve (AUC) of ZNF667-AS1 for diagnosing HBV-related HCC from CHB reached 0.841. miR-210-3p was validated as a direct target of ZNF667-AS1, and a significant negative correlation was observed between their expression levels. Overexpression of ZNF667-AS1 inhibited the proliferation, migration, and invasion of HCC cells, whereas this inhibitory effect was reversed by transfection with miR-210-3p mimic. LncRNA ZNF667-AS1 is downregulated in HBV-related HCC and exerts in vitro tumor‐suppressive effects by targeting miR-210-3p to upregulate CPEB2 expression, thus providing a potential auxiliary biomarker for HBV-related HCC diagnosis and a novel regulatory axis for understanding disease pathogenesis.
abstract_zh: 探讨长链非编码RNA(lncRNA)ZNF667-AS1在乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)相关肝细胞癌(HCC)中的生物学功能、临床意义和调控机制。本研究纳入了 107 名 HBV 相关 HCC 患者、105 名 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 患者和 105 名健康对照者。采用实时定量聚合酶链反应(RT-qPCR)检测ZNF667-AS1、miR-210-3p、CPEB2的表达水平。分析ZNF667-AS1表达与患者临床特征的关联,并进行受试者工作特征(ROC)曲线分析以评估其诊断价值。进行生物信息学预测和双荧光素酶报告基因测定,以验证 ZNF667-AS1 和 miR-210-3p 之间以及 miR-210-3p 和 CPEB2 之间的靶向关联。应用细胞计数试剂盒-8 (CCK-8) 和 Transwell 检测来评估细胞转染后 HCC 细胞的生物学功能。在 HBV 相关 HCC 患者的组织样本和 HBV 相关 HCC 细胞系中,ZNF667-AS1 和 CPEB2 的表达水平显着下调。ROC曲线分析显示,ZNF667-AS1诊断CHB与HBV相关HCC的曲线下面积(AUC)达到0.841。miR-210-3p被验证为ZNF667-AS1的直接靶标,并且观察到它们的表达水平之间存在显着的负相关。ZNF667-AS1 的过表达抑制 HCC 细胞的增殖、迁移和侵袭,而这种抑制作用可通过转染 miR-210-3p 模拟物而逆转。LncRNA ZNF667-AS1 在 HBV 相关 HCC 中下调,并通过靶向 miR-210-3p 上调 CPEB2 表达发挥体外肿瘤抑制作用,从而为 HBV 相关 HCC 诊断 提供潜在的辅助生物标志物,并为理解疾病 诊断 提供新的调控轴。

title: Diagnostic performance of liver biochemical and hemostatic markers for assessing cirrhosis severity in chronic hepatitis B
abstract: This study aimed to explore the utility of liver biochemical and hemostatic (including coagulation, anticoagulation, and fibrinolysis) markers for assessing cirrhosis severity in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients. In this current study, a total of 28 healthy controls and 78 patients with CHB-related cirrhosis were enrolled. Routine laboratory markers including platelet count (PLT), albumin (ALB), total bilirubin (TBIL), creatinine (CREA), prothrombin time (PT), activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT), factor VIII (FVIII), prothrombin activity (PA), protein S (PS), protein C (PC), antithrombin III (AT-III) and D-dimer (D-D) were measured. Correlations between the measured parameters and Child-Pugh score (CPS)/ Model for End-Stage Liver Disease score (MELD) were also explored. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to evaluate the ability of these indicators to discriminate between mild and moderate-to-severe CHB-related cirrhosis. Patients with CHB-related cirrhosis exhibited significantly lower levels of ALB, PA, PS, PC, AT-III, and PLT, and significantly higher levels of TBIL, PT, APTT, FVIII, and D-D, compared with healthy controls ( p < 0.05). ALB, PA, AT-III, PS, and PC showed significant negative correlations with both CPS and MELD ( p < 0.01). TBIL, PT, and APTT demonstrated significant positive correlations ( p < 0.01). ROC curve analysis revealed that AT-III achieved an AUC of 0.95 (95% CI: 0.88–1.00) for distinguishing cirrhosis severity, followed by PC (AUC: 0.87) and PA (AUC: 0.87). As expected, Child-Pugh components (ALB, TBIL, PT) showed strong associations with the score. Among markers not incorporated into the CPS, AT-III is significantly associated with the severity of CHB-related cirrhosis and exhibits promising discriminatory ability for staging CHB-related cirrhosis. It may support a low-cost, objective framework for dynamic monitoring of HBV-related cirrhosis progression. Although ALB, TBIL, and PT were also correlated with disease severity, these associations are subject to incorporation bias and thus represent confirmatory rather than novel findings.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) leads to cirrhosis, but noninvasive markers for assessing its severity are limited. This study asked whether liver biochemical and hemostatic markers can objectively stage CHB-related cirrhosis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study enrolled 28 healthy controls and 78 patients with CHB-related cirrhosis to evaluate diagnostic markers.
analysis.methods: Routine laboratory markers including platelet count, albumin, total bilirubin, creatinine, prothrombin time, activated partial thromboplastin time, factor VIII, prothrombin activity, protein S, protein C, antithrombin III and D-dimer were measured. Correlations with Child-Pugh and MELD scores were explored, and ROC curve analysis assessed discrimination between mild and moderate-to-severe cirrhosis.
analysis.main_results: Patients with CHB-related cirrhosis had significantly lower albumin, prothrombin activity, protein S, protein C, antithrombin III and platelet count, and significantly higher total bilirubin, prothrombin time, activated partial thromboplastin time, factor VIII and D-dimer than healthy controls (p < 0.05). Antithrombin III showed the highest area under the ROC curve (0.95, 95% CI 0.88–1.00) for distinguishing cirrhosis severity, followed by protein C and prothrombin activity (each AUC 0.87).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Antithrombin III was significantly associated with CHB-related cirrhosis severity and showed strong discriminatory ability for staging, whereas albumin, total bilirubin and prothrombin time associations reflected incorporation bias and were confirmatory rather than novel.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest antithrombin III could enable low-cost, objective monitoring of HBV-related cirrhosis progression in clinical practice.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The cross-sectional design and small sample limit causal inference and generalisability; evidence strength is moderate due to potential selection bias and unadjusted confounding.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study evaluated whether liver biochemical and hemostatic markers can stage cirrhosis severity in 78 patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB)-related cirrhosis and 28 healthy controls. Routine markers including albumin, prothrombin activity, protein S, protein C, antithrombin III, platelet count, total bilirubin, prothrombin time, activated partial thromboplastin time, factor VIII and D-dimer were measured. Patients with cirrhosis showed significantly lower levels of albumin, prothrombin activity, protein S, protein C, antithrombin III and platelet count, and higher levels of total bilirubin, prothrombin time, activated partial thromboplastin time, factor VIII and D-dimer than controls. Antithrombin III achieved the highest area under the ROC curve (0.95) for distinguishing cirrhosis severity, followed by protein C and prothrombin activity (each 0.87). The authors interpret antithrombin III as a promising marker for staging CHB-related cirrhosis, while noting that associations of albumin, total bilirubin and prothrombin time reflect incorporation bias. title_zh: 慢性乙型肝炎 肝脏生化和止血标志物评估肝硬化严重程度的诊断性能
source_body_en: This study aimed to explore the utility of liver biochemical and hemostatic (including coagulation, anticoagulation, and fibrinolysis) markers for assessing cirrhosis severity in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients. In this current study, a total of 28 healthy controls and 78 patients with CHB-related cirrhosis were enrolled. Routine laboratory markers including platelet count (PLT), albumin (ALB), total bilirubin (TBIL), creatinine (CREA), prothrombin time (PT), activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT), factor VIII (FVIII), prothrombin activity (PA), protein S (PS), protein C (PC), antithrombin III (AT-III) and D-dimer (D-D) were measured. Correlations between the measured parameters and Child-Pugh score (CPS)/ Model for End-Stage Liver Disease score (MELD) were also explored. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to evaluate the ability of these indicators to discriminate between mild and moderate-to-severe CHB-related cirrhosis. Patients with CHB-related cirrhosis exhibited significantly lower levels of ALB, PA, PS, PC, AT-III, and PLT, and significantly higher levels of TBIL, PT, APTT, FVIII, and D-D, compared with healthy controls ( p < 0.05). ALB, PA, AT-III, PS, and PC showed significant negative correlations with both CPS and MELD ( p < 0.01). TBIL, PT, and APTT demonstrated significant positive correlations ( p < 0.01). ROC curve analysis revealed that AT-III achieved an AUC of 0.95 (95% CI: 0.88–1.00) for distinguishing cirrhosis severity, followed by PC (AUC: 0.87) and PA (AUC: 0.87). As expected, Child-Pugh components (ALB, TBIL, PT) showed strong associations with the score. Among markers not incorporated into the CPS, AT-III is significantly associated with the severity of CHB-related cirrhosis and exhibits promising discriminatory ability for staging CHB-related cirrhosis. It may support a low-cost, objective framework for dynamic monitoring of HBV-related cirrhosis progression. Although ALB, TBIL, and PT were also correlated with disease severity, these associations are subject to incorporation bias and thus represent confirmatory rather than novel findings.
abstract_zh: 本研究旨在探讨肝脏生化和止血(包括凝血、抗凝和纤溶)标志物在评估 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 患者肝硬化严重程度方面的效用。在本研究中,共有 28 名健康对照者和 78 名患有 CHB 相关肝硬化的患者入组。测量常规实验室指标,包括血小板计数(PLT)、白蛋白(ALB)、总胆红素(TBIL)、肌酐(CREA)、凝血酶原时间(PT)、活化部分凝血活酶时间(APTT)、因子VIII(FVIII)、凝血酶原活性(PA)、蛋白S(PS)、蛋白C(PC)、抗凝血酶III(AT-III)和D-二聚体(D-D)。还探讨了测量参数与 Child-Pugh 评分 (CPS)/终末期肝病模型评分 (MELD) 之间的相关性。进行受试者工作特征 (ROC) 曲线分析,以评估这些指标区分轻度和中度至重度 CHB 相关肝硬化的能力。与健康对照相比,CHB 相关肝硬化患者的 ALB、PA、PS、PC、AT-III 和 PLT 水平显着降低,而 TBIL、PT、APTT、FVIII 和 D-D 水平显着升高 (p < 0.05)。ALB、PA、AT-III、PS 和 PC 与 CPS 和 MELD 均呈显着负相关 (p < 0.01)。TBIL、PT 和 APTT 表现出显着的正相关性 (p < 0.01)。ROC曲线分析显示,AT-III区分肝硬化严重程度的AUC为0.95(95% CI:0.88-1.00),其次是PC(AUC:0.87)和PA(AUC:0.87)。正如预期的那样,Child-Pugh 成分(ALB、TBIL、PT)与分数显示出很强的关联性。在未纳入 CPS 的标志物中,AT-III 与 CHB 相关肝硬化的严重程度显着相关,并且在 CHB 相关肝硬化分期方面表现出有希望的区分能力。它可能支持动态监测 HBV 相关肝硬化进展的低成本、客观框架。尽管 ALB、TBIL 和 PT 也与疾病严重程度相关,但这些关联会受到合并偏倚的影响,因此代表的是证实性而非新颖的发现。

title: CXCL16 gene promoter methylation is associated with inflammation in patients with chronic hepatitis B
abstract: Abstract Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection causes persistent hepatic inflammation, and chemokine CXCL16 serves as a key mediator in liver injury, but its epigenetic regulation in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains unclear. This study enrolled 217 CHB patients (113 HBeAg‐positive, 104 HBeAg‐negative) and 27 healthy controls to investigate CXCL16 promoter methylation, mRNA and protein expression, as well as their correlations with inflammatory indices and liver injury markers. The results showed that CXCL16 promoter methylation was significantly lower, while CXCL16 mRNA and serum levels were markedly higher in CHB patients, especially in HBeAg‐positive cases. CXCL16 promoter methylation was negatively correlated with CXCL16 expression, HBeAg status, ALT, AST, TNF‐α and IL‐1βlevels. ROC analysis indicated that CXCL16 promoter methylation had favorable diagnostic value for evaluating hepatic inflammatory injury in CHB patients. In conclusion, CXCL16 promoter hypomethylation is closely associated with elevated CXCL16 expression and exacerbated hepatic inflammation in CHB patients, and may serve as a potential non‐invasive biomarker for assessing CHB‐related liver inflammation. These findings enrich the epigenetic mechanism underlying HBV‐related hepatic inflammation and provide a novel target which is CXCL16 for clinical evaluation and intervention.

title_zh: CXCL16基因启动子甲基化与慢性乙型肝炎患者的炎症相关
source_body_en: Abstract Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection causes persistent hepatic inflammation, and chemokine CXCL16 serves as a key mediator in liver injury, but its epigenetic regulation in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains unclear. This study enrolled 217 CHB patients (113 HBeAg‐positive, 104 HBeAg‐negative) and 27 healthy controls to investigate CXCL16 promoter methylation, mRNA and protein expression, as well as their correlations with inflammatory indices and liver injury markers. The results showed that CXCL16 promoter methylation was significantly lower, while CXCL16 mRNA and serum levels were markedly higher in CHB patients, especially in HBeAg‐positive cases. CXCL16 promoter methylation was negatively correlated with CXCL16 expression, HBeAg status, ALT, AST, TNF‐α and IL‐1βlevels. ROC analysis indicated that CXCL16 promoter methylation had favorable diagnostic value for evaluating hepatic inflammatory injury in CHB patients. In conclusion, CXCL16 promoter hypomethylation is closely associated with elevated CXCL16 expression and exacerbated hepatic inflammation in CHB patients, and may serve as a potential non‐invasive biomarker for assessing CHB‐related liver inflammation. These findings enrich the epigenetic mechanism underlying HBV‐related hepatic inflammation and provide a novel target which is CXCL16 for clinical evaluation and intervention.

title: Biopsy-Based Head-to-Head Comparison of Eight Non-Invasive Fibrosis Scores in Treatment-Naïve Chronic Hepatitis B
abstract: Abstract Background and Aims Accurate fibrosis staging is essential for managing chronic hepatitis B (CHB). Although several non-invasive fibrosis scores have been proposed as alternatives to liver biopsy, their comparative performance across fibrosis stages remains uncertain. This study compared eight commonly used non-invasive fibrosis scores for detecting significant, advanced, and severe fibrosis in treatment-naïve patients with CHB. Materials and Methods This retrospective study included treatment-naïve patients with CHB who underwent liver biopsy between May 2017 and May 2024. Fibrosis was staged using the Ishak scoring system. APRI, FIB-4, KING, GUCI, AAR, API, INPR, and GPR were evaluated for detecting F ≥ 2, F ≥ 3, and F ≥ 4 fibrosis using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Optimal cut-off values were determined using the Youden index. AUROC, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value were calculated. Pairwise AUROC comparisons were performed using DeLong's test. Results A total of 268 patients were included. All scores showed poor performance for detecting significant fibrosis (F ≥ 2), with AUROC values below 0.60. Diagnostic accuracy improved for advanced and severe fibrosis. KING achieved the highest AUROC for advanced fibrosis (0.807), followed by FIB-4 (0.797), whereas GPR showed the highest AUROC for severe fibrosis (0.929). DeLong analysis demonstrated no significant differences among the best-performing scores. Conclusion None of the evaluated scores demonstrated sufficient accuracy to replace liver biopsy for detecting significant fibrosis. However, FIB-4, KING, and GPR showed good performance for advanced and severe fibrosis and may be useful for initial risk stratification and identifying patients who require further evaluation with liver biopsy.

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景和目的 准确的纤维化分期对于治疗 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 至关重要。尽管已提出几种非侵入性纤维化评分作为肝活检的替代方法,但它们在纤维化阶段的比较表现仍不确定。这项研究比较了八种常用的非侵入性纤维化评分,用于检测 治疗 初治慢性乙型肝炎患者的显着、晚期和严重纤维化。材料和方法 这项回顾性研究纳入了 2017 年 5 月至 2024 年 5 月期间接受肝活检的 治疗 初治慢性乙型肝炎患者。使用 Ishak 评分系统对纤维化进行分期。使用接受者操作特征 (ROC) 分析评估 APRI、FIB-4、KING、GUCI、AAR、API、INPR 和 GPR 检测 F ≥ 2、F ≥ 3 和 F ≥ 4 纤维化的情况。使用约登指数确定最佳截止值。计算AUROC、敏感性、特异性、阳性预测值和阴性预测值。使用 DeLong 检验进行成对 AUROC 比较。结果共纳入268例患者。所有评分在检测显着纤维化(F ≥ 2)方面表现不佳,AUROC 值低于 0.60。晚期和严重纤维化的诊断准确性得到提高。KING 在晚期纤维化方面取得了最高的 AUROC (0.807),其次是 FIB-4 (0.797),而 GPR 在严重纤维化方面取得了最高的 AUROC (0.929)。德隆分析表明,表现最好的分数之间没有显着差异。结论 评估的评分均未表现出足够的准确性来替代肝活检来检测显着的纤维化。然而,FIB-4、KING 和 GPR 在晚期和严重纤维化方面表现出良好的性能,可能有助于初步风险分层和识别需要肝活检进一步评估的患者。
